attorneys.name: Barbara J. Aaby
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Lake Oswego, OR
attorneys.bio:
Barbara Aaby graduated with Honors from Ohio State University (Summa Cum Laude) in 1973. She was the recipient of the Maternal and Child Health Scholarship Award and pursued graduate studies at Case Western Reserve University earning a degree in Social Science Administration. In 1993, she obtained her law degree from Lewis and Clark College Northwestern School of Law.

Barbara’s early years were spent on a small dairy farm in Ohio and this experience gave her an understanding of the challenges of organic farming and a healthy respect for nature. Barbara has hiked many, if not most, of the trails in the Columbia River Gorge and she even managed to hike the Pacific Coast Trail on Vancouver Island. She and her family frequently spend time camping on Mt. Hood, biking on bike trails throughout Oregon and gardening.

Barbara has been a member of the Oregon State Bar since 1993 and is a member of a number of legal organizations, including Oregon Women Lawyers and the Washington County Bar Association. Barbara has in the past served as the Chair of the American Bar Association Committee on Child Custody. She is a contributing author to the Oregon State Bar Family Law Continuing Legal Education Book and has authored topics such as the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction Act and parenting plans.

Barbara has in the past served as a volunteer judge for the High School Mock Trial Program as well as the Mock Trial program hosted by Lewis and Clark College. Barbara serves on the Board of Trustees for the Washington County NAMI (National Association of Mental Illness) and is a strong supporter of providing mental health services for adolescents as well as adults.

attorneys.name: Dean E. Aldrich
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Lawyers in West Linn, OR
attorneys.bio:
Dean Aldrich received his law degree, cum laude, from Tulane University, and received his undergraduate degree in civil engineering, with high scholarship, from Oregon State University. During college, Dean worked in heavy highway construction and building construction. After graduating from college, Dean was a project manager for an international building construction company based out of Portland, Oregon. Dean then traveled to New Orleans to attend law school at Tulane. In addition to graduating with honors, Dean was a member of the Tulane National Moot Court team that swept the southeast regional tournament, and advanced to the finals in New York City.

After graduating from law school, Dean focused his legal career on complex litigation. Dean has successfully handled complex trials and arbitrations involving a variety of claims (environmental, trade secrets, construction payment and delay, product liability, construction defect, business, water use, insurance coverage, government liability).

With regard to construction claims, Dean has been involved in resolving significant construction disputes in Oregon, negotiating multi-million dollar settlements, as well as obtaining an $11.8 million dollar jury verdict in a construction defect trial in Multnomah County. Dean also prevailed in a complex insurance coverage trial that has significant impacts for all construction defect cases in Oregon. Further, Dean has regularly handled breach of contract, payment and delay disputes from all sides (owner, contractor, subcontractor, supplier, architect, consultant) throughout his career, for claims large and small, complex and straightforward, and during boom and bust cycles.

With regard to product liability cases, Dean has successfully defended domestic and foreign manufacturers and distributors in a variety of complex product liability cases in state and federal court involving automobiles, ATVs, motorcycles, engine components, machinery, asbestos, building products, and recalled products. Dean has also prosecuted product liability claims involving a variety of products, achieving significant jury verdicts.

Dean also has served as general counsel for several companies, and has resolved all manner of business disputes. Dean has also drafted and negotiated complex business and construction contracts nationwide.

Dean is an AV Peer Review Rated attorney according to the Martindale-Hubbell Legal Ability and General Ethics Standards Rating system, which is a century-long tradition for rating lawyers. Based on the confidential opinions of lawyers and judges, Dean is recognized as pre-eminent, and has reached the height of professional excellence and the highest levels of skill and integrity. Dean is also recognized by Best Lawyers.

Dean is a member of numerous legal organizations and construction/engineering organizations, and is a frequent speaker on construction litigation. Dean is active in the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association and has testified before the Oregon Legislature on construction law issues. Dean is also often sought out as a construction law expert by the local news media.

Awards and Honors

Honors

attorneys.name: David N. Allen
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in West Linn, OR
attorneys.bio:
David has practiced law for over three decades, including with the Oregon Department of Justice, in private practice, and as legal counsel for public entities. Most recently, David served as city attorney for a coastal municipality, and before that as an elected city council member for over 13 years.

David is originally from the Chicago area and moved to the Pacific Northwest to attend college and law school, graduating from Lewis & Clark Law School in 1985. He has lived on the central coast in Newport for close to 30 years, and has traveled the length of the Oregon coast many times over, in particular while serving for over 12 years as a governor-appointed member of a state advisory council on ocean/coastal policy issues.

In his spare time, David can be seen walking his malamute-husky on the beaches around Newport.

attorneys.name: Andrew M. Altschul
attorneys.practice_type: Discrimination Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Andrew Altschul practiced labor and employment law at two of the country's largest law firms for almost a decade before opening his own employment law boutique in 2004. Andrew has substantial experience representing both employers and employees in all aspects of employment disputes. He provides day-to-day counseling on employment issues, collective bargaining representation, and serves as a mediator on labor and employment matters. Andrew also has a national ERISA benefit litigation practice and regularly litigates ERISA actions throughout the country. Andrew is recognized in The Best Lawyers of America, Oregon Super Lawyers and Rising Stars, and selected as a leader in his field for Oregon by Chambers USA. He served as the Chair of the Oregon State Bar Board of Bar Examiners, which is responsible for designing and grading the Oregon Bar Examination and has received Senior Professional in Human Resources (SPHR) certification from the Human Resources Certification Institute (HRCI). Andrew is also a frequent speaker at national and local employment law forums. Andrew is a member of the Oregon, Washington and California bars. He received his law degree from the University of Michigan Law School and his bachelor's degree from Grinnell College.

attorneys.name: Kelly L Andersen
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Protection Lawyers in Medford, OR
attorneys.bio:
Continuing Education:

Mr. Andersen has continued to be current in personal injury law by regularly attending state and national continuing legal education courses, taking far more classes than the law requires. His continuing education has included trial advocacy seminars at Stanford and Harvard Universities, as well as courses taken in San Francisco, Chicago, San Diego, Monterey, Toronto and, of course, at various locations in Oregon.

He has also lectured at seminars on the subject of personal injury law and has written and published in scholarly journals.

Practice:

Mr. Andersen is admitted to practice in both State and Federal Courts, and has served as lead counsel for people injured in Oregon, California, Washington and Hawaii. He has also handled cases in the Oregon Court of Appeals, the Oregon Supreme Court, the U.S. Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals (covering the Western United States), and the U.S. court of Claims.

In 2007, Mr. Andersen was named as one of Oregon's "Super Lawyers" from the publishers of Law and Politics. In the selection process, Law and Politics invited more than 10,000 Oregon Lawyers to participate in the nominating process and each candidate so named was subjected to exhaustive peer review. In the field of general plaintiff personal injury, Mr. Andersen was selected in the top 25 attorneys in the entire state of Oregon, only four of whom practiced outside the Portland area. Mr. Andersen was the only attorney selected for this prestigious honor in the entire southern half of the state.

Mr. Andersen has also been inducted into the "Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum," a rare honor reserved for attorneys who have achieved multi-million dollar settlements or verdicts. This forum only came into existence in 2007 and recognized past achievements.

attorneys.name: Carolyn A Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Disputes (Plaintiff and Defendant) Lawyers in Ashland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Carolyn has specialized in labor and employment law since 1990. She is a graduate of Yale University and the University of California, Hastings College of the Law. She's licensed to practice law in Oregon, and she is an inactive member of the California State Bar. Carolyn represents plaintiffs and defendants in wrongful termination, sexual harassment, discrimination and wage claims. She advises employers on how to avoid these claims, and helps negotiate employment, independent contractor and severance agreements. She handles unemployment appeals and other administrative hearings. Carolyn also works with start-up businesses, creating corporations and LLCs, and advising clients on how to get their new business up and running; she regularly handles business sales and purchases.

Education and Experience

Carolyn grew up in Rhode Island and moved west after graduating from Yale in 1984 with a degree in History. After attending law school at Hastings in San Francisco, she practiced briefly in Seattle and returned to the Bay Area to work in labor and employment law. She spent nine years with Neyhart, Anderson, Freitas, Flynn & Grosboll in San Francisco, representing labor unions in the building trades and public transit industries.

Founding Anderson Bradley Krant

At Anderson Bradley Krant, Carolyn represents both plaintiffs and defendants in employment disputes, specializing in wrongful termination, sexual harassment, discrimination, whistleblower and overtime claims. She counsels employers on how to avoid such claims, and she helps employers draft a wide range of agreements, including independent contractor agreements and severance agreements. Carolyn has many clients in health care, freight logistics, in-home care services, and in manufacturing industries. She offers a wide range of services, including business purchase and sale transactions, business formations, and representation (for both plaintiff and defense) in civil litigation. "I see people coming to the Rogue Valley to start new businesses, and they have no idea where to begin. They're faced with questions of corporate formation and employment issues. attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense / DUI Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Drew Anderson is a skilled criminal defense attorney who represents clients facing serious charges from the firm’s Portland office. His practice centers on protecting the rights of individuals accused of offenses such as DUII and other misdemeanor and felony crimes. Drew is known for his thorough case preparation and his commitment to keeping clients informed, confident, and supported throughout the legal process.

Before transitioning to defense work, Drew built a strong foundation as a prosecutor. He served as a Deputy District Attorney in Marion County, where he handled a wide range of cases involving property offenses, drug-related charges, and Measure 11 person crimes. Earlier in his career, he worked as a Deputy District Attorney in Coos County, gaining valuable trial experience in a rural court system that required adaptability and hands-on litigation skills. This prosecutorial background allows Drew to anticipate opposing strategies and develop effective defense plans.

Drew earned his undergraduate degree in History and American Studies from the University of Idaho and completed his legal education at Willamette University College of Law. Prior to law school, he gained unique life experience working in Alaska’s fishing industry and later with a nonprofit organization in Southeast Asia, where he supported construction initiatives and taught English. These experiences shaped his strong work ethic and global perspective.

Outside of his legal practice, Drew values time with his wife and daughter and enjoys outdoor and recreational activities, including skiing, hunting, fishing, and golf.

attorneys.bio:
Practice Focus

The best attorneys are problem solvers. My law practice focuses on finding effective solutions for both public and private employers in the defense of claims involving discrimination, harassment, wrongful discharge, violations of medical leave laws, workers' compensation retaliation, and wage-and-hour claims.

I have successfully defended numerous claims in all of these areas, including claims filed with the Oregon Bureau of Labor & Industries ("BOLI") and with the federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission ("EEOC").

I also negotiate and draft employment and other business contracts, severance agreements and personnel handbooks, as well as give advice on hiring, firing and layoffs. Internal investigations of employee complaints are a mainstay of my practice.

A major component of my practice is problem solving and prevention. To that end, I advise employers on how to train managers and supervisors to recognize potential discrimination or retaliation complaints before they become a reality. I help employers avoid wage claims by making sure employees are properly classified in accordance with state and federal law. I have extensive experience interpreting and implementing family medical leave laws and the Americans with Disabilities Act ("ADA").

In addition, I have a wealth of experience in labor law, having advised both public and private employers in negotiations, contract enforcement and resolution of grievances, including unfair labor practice complaints.

attorneys.name: Lauren M. Barnhart
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Lauren Barnhart grew up in Tacoma, Washington with her mom, three brothers and a village of aunts and uncles. Lauren learned at an early age that hard work and creative solutions can allow you to overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles. Lauren realized early on that she would need to find her own way to pay for college, so by her senior year, she had secured a full-ride music scholarship to a four-year university, and performed in Carnegie Hall as the principal bassoonist in the Tacoma Youth Symphony.

Lauren entered law school with lofty ambitions of bringing international war criminals to justice but soon realized that she felt the greatest reward serving individuals within her own community. Practicing family law allows Lauren the opportunity to help families navigate through what is arguably the most difficult time of their lives. Practicing estate planning allows Lauren to help families plan for their future. When Lauren meets a client for the first time, she wants them to know above all else that their case matters to her, and that she can get them through to the other side.

Lauren practices law with integrity and compassion and believes that when dealing with families, the best outcomes are not measured by winners and losers, rather equitable solutions and child-focused results. While Lauren does maintain a successful and active litigation practice, she will first try and explore all opportunities for settlement to avoid litigation. Coming from a modest background, Lauren truly appreciates the price tag, and her goal is always to reach the most equitable outcome, as expeditiously and efficiently as possible.

Lauren moved from Washington to Oregon in 2007 and has been living in Portland since shortly after graduating cum laude from Willamette University College of Law in 2012. In her free time, Lauren enjoys spending time with her husband and spoiled border collie (Dolly Parton), watching movies, camping, wine tasting, playing modern and classic euro board games, and singing karaoke. Lauren’s favorite thing about Portland is the proximity to so many types of activities. She loves that you can access the desert, the mountains, the coast or the river all with only an hour or two drive. Then when you get back, you can take advantage of Portland’s diverse food scene, vast array of breweries and urban wineries, eco-conscious transportation, self-sufficient neighborhoods, and a lively alternative music scene.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Newport, OR
attorneys.bio:
Brent Barton represents children with brain injuries, particularly babies injured during birth because of medical malpractice. He litigates these cases all over Oregon.

Brent is an extremely detail-oriented attorney who works with medical experts to establish how birth injuries harmed his clients. He then works with expert lifecare planners to establish what his clients need to realize their greatest potential. Brent also works with professional fiduciaries to ensure his clients remain supported and protected throughout their lives.

Brent has recovered over $175 million for clients in verdicts or settlements, including more than 30 cases in excess of $1,000,000. He holds degrees from Harvard Law School, Stanford University, and Cambridge University.

Community service is important to Brent, who previously served in the Oregon Legislature. Brent continues this work by representing many nonprofit organizations pro bono.

attorneys.name: Mark R. Barzda
attorneys.practice_type: Military Divorce Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
For Mark, being a family law attorney means providing quality care and guidance to his clients during one of the most traumatic times of their lives—and sometimes be their source of hope when times seem so hopeless. Those who know Mark well describe him as a dedicated, caring, and hard-working advocate for his clients. For Mark, the best part about practicing family law is believing he can have a positive impact on the clients and families he represents. He is a team player and strong believer in the success of negotiating family law issues between the parties in an honorable and cost-effective matter. Mark enjoys interacting with his clients to help them emerge from a time in their life that can be quite traumatic. His goal is to always help them not only traverse their legal issues, but to also transition successfully into post married life.

In recent years Mark has seen his practice expand such that he has navigated many high-asset divorce cases and complex custody and parenting time cases, both through alternative dispute resolution options and through litigation. Mark strives to help each case settle outside of court through creative solutions and collaborative practice; however, when a matter cannot settle, Mark has navigated his clients through complex litigation with successful results.

Mark is the proud father of three and loves to spend time with his children. He is an avid collector of film and music and comic books and boasts a film collection of over 4000 movies and comic book collection of over 10,000 titles. As a fan of the study of history and foreign culture, he previously undertook the academic pursuit of a degree in Art History and has traveled extensively throughout the world. His life-long mission is to make the most of life, to have a positive impact on the people around him, to care, to leave a legacy, and most importantly to be the best father he can be to his children.

attorneys.name: William A. Barton
attorneys.practice_type: Serious Injury Claims Lawyers in Newport, OR
attorneys.bio:
Bill is, by anyone’s description, one of the best plaintiff’s litigators in the country. He began his significant mark on the legal landscape by bringing the first suit against the Boy Scouts of America that did not settle out of court but went to trial – a landmark case that helped to break open the field of psychological injury. He went on to become the first attorney to sue the Vatican for sexual abuse by clergy.

Bill authored the definitive book on psychological injury cases, sharing his knowledge and experience to the benefit of countless lawyers and their injured clients. He has practiced law for over 40 years, continuing to try difficult and challenging cases, while remaining highly active in the professional community, serving on many boards, writing, and teaching. He has lectured on trial advocacy in 35 state sand 4 countries and testified as an expert witness in legal malpractice cases.

attorneys.name: Merrill J. Baumann
attorneys.practice_type: Business Transactions Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Merrill is an experienced and dynamic business and technology attorney, with a legal career spanning over three decades in Oregon, California, and abroad. His experience in representing local and international clients, in such varied industries as technology, software, gaming, manufacturing, consumer and food products, and distribution, has given him a breadth of experience and expertise that is unique in Portland. His representation of tech and creative clients includes substantial intellectual property work, from structuring complex licensing transactions to protection of ideas, creative works, and brands, with trademark and copyright strategies and prosecution of infringers of his clients’ valuable IP assets. Merrill has worked on and led M+A transactions in a myriad of industries, and with transaction values as high as $1 billion. He has represented corporate clients regarding climate change regulations and opportunities and has handled numerous greenhouse gas offset purchases and sales.

Prior to relocating to Oregon, Merrill was posted to his California firm’s Tokyo office, where he represented multinational corporations in international finance, distribution, and M+A transactions. In addition to representing private clients, Merrill had the honor to serve as general counsel to his prior firm in California, responsible for overseeing and budgeting the firm’s legal matters.

Outside the office, Merrill enjoys cycling and visits with family in New York City and South Africa. Merrill is also a passionate supporter the arts, as a frequent board member for Oregon arts organizations, and a member of an 80+ member choral group in the Portland area. He also interviews ambitious high school students in their pursuit of attending his own alma mater, Dartmouth College.

attorneys.name: Chase A.S. Beguin
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Grants Pass, OR
attorneys.bio:
Chase A.S. Beguin is our business litigator for the firm. He grew up in Coastal North Carolina before attending Darlington School Soccer Academy in Georgia for high school. He graduated from Guilford College in Greensboro, North Carolina in 2017 with a bachelors degree in Business Management and Health Sciences. After a year working out of school, he enrolled in Elon University School of Law, and graduated in 2021 with an emphasis on business and corporate law. During his time at law school, he was armed with practical experience in a wide variety of corporate and business law through his work with Elon’s Small Business and Entrepreneurship Clinic.

Chase was drawn to the Southern Oregon area after law school due to its vast nature preserves, its rural character, and its high concentration of businesses of all sizes in the Rogue Valley.

Since his admission to the Oregon State Bar in 2022, he has embalmed himself with his litigation practice, specializing in complex business litigation; while providing counseling and litigation support on matters relating to estate planning, land use, and matters which implicate Oregon’s anti-SLAPP statute.

Chase also utilizes his litigation experience to inform his counseling on transactional document drafting to ensure the best protection, and overall service, for the respective needs of his clients.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey C. Bodie
attorneys.practice_type: Intellectual Property Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Bodie’s practice focuses upon counseling business and real estate clients on a broad spectrum of issues with which they must deal in order to successfully compete and expand in today’s economic and regulatory climate.

Mr. Bodie counsels owners of real estate, intellectual property and businesses ranging from technology to manufacturing, distribution, real estate and service-based businesses. Mr. Bodie structures transactions to address the needs and circumstances of clients, whether they be startup, emerging growth, cloud-based, or mature businesses.

Drawing on his 40 years of experience, Mr. Bodie assists clients in the identification, protection, commercialization and enforcement of intellectual property rights. He counsels clients in the prosecution and procurement of federal copyright, trademark and servicemark registrations and advises regarding the identification and safeguarding of proprietary information via trade secret protection programs. Mr. Bodie provides strategies for commercializing his clients’ intellectual property via licensing of trademarks, copyrights, patents and trade secrets. He has substantial experience in negotiation of software license agreements (in OEM, company-wide, site-wide or end-user contexts) with applications ranging from process control software used in the petrochemical industry to commercial debt recovery to productivity software. Mr. Bodie has negotiated purchase agreements for design and utility patents and has structured such transactions as option (allowing time for due diligence) acquisition and invention assignment agreements. He has negotiated software development, joint authorship, and source code escrow agreements. Mr. Bodie has experience in the commercialization of manufacturing and/or marketing rights under patent (both utility and design), trade secret or trademark licenses. Mr. Bodie assists clients in commercializing their intellectual property via cloud platform (i.e. SaaS) by drafting required Privacy Policies and Terms of Service.

Mr. Bodie’s substantial experience in real estate transactions encompasses the sale/acquisition/development of commercial property, commercial broker representation and leasing activity from ground leases to professional office, commercial, retail, industrial and manufacturing leases. His development experience includes negotiation of agreements with lenders, architects and contractors. Mr. Bodie has experience in §1031 tax deferred exchanges. He has prepared real estate brokerage and management agreements. Mr. Bodie is experienced in counseling clients on business formation and choice of entity. He has negotiated agreements required by start-up, high growth, or mature businesses including key person employment, commercial loan transactions, equipment purchases, strategic partner arrangements, and independent contractor, sales representative, distributor and nondisclosure/noncompete agreements. Mr. Bodie has substantial experience in the sale or acquisition of business assets, capital stock or LLC membership interests, joint venture agreements and partnership agreements. He advises clients on matters of corporate and LLC governance.

Mr. Bodie also enjoys counseling business and real estate clients on short and long term strategic planning issues, particularly since he is able to provide the perspective of both transactional and lawyer and former litigator.

Mr. Bodie has previously had substantial real estate and business litigation experience. His real estate experience includes: foreclosure (trust deed, mortgage or construction lien); receivership; specific performance and rescission; commercial lease disputes; condemnation; commercial brokerage and property management disputes; fraud; constructive trusts; boundary disputes; trespass and commercial landlord-tenant issues. Mr. Bodie’s business litigation experience includes: breach of contract; fraud; breach of fiduciary duty; corporate litigation including takeover issues.

attorneys.name: Bryan Boender
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Eugene, OR
attorneys.bio:
Bryan Boender is a criminal defense attorney with trial experience in federal, state, and municipal courts. Bryan has defended those accused of major crimes, as well as felony and misdemeanor offenses. His experience includes defending complex criminal cases, such as aggravated murder, murder, manslaughter, sex crimes, Measure 11 offenses, and domestic violence crimes. Bryan's practice includes defending both felony and misdemeanor driving under the influence (DUII) cases.

As the founding partner of Boender & Payment, Attorneys, Bryan leads the firm's criminal defense practice. He believes that skilled advocates must continue to participate in focused criminal defense training throughout their careers. He has attended two of the most prestigious advanced training programs for criminal defense lawyers: the National Criminal Defense College and the National College of Capital Voir Dire. Bryan has also published written materials and been a conference speaker on complex criminal defense topics, including death penalty defense, justice involved veterans, and sex crimes defense.

Bryan is an Afghanistan combat veteran. He served on active duty and overseas with the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division in the 508th Parachute Infantry Regiment. Bryan continues to give back to the veterans community, and he is among the founding attorneys of the Veterans Legal Clinic in Eugene, Oregon. The clinic has served veterans in need of legal services since 2012.

Bryan lives in Eugene, Oregon with his wife Amanda.

attorneys.name: Thomas M. Brasier
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Tom Brasier is a highly qualified Family-Law attorney in Portland, OR and Vancouver, WA. Mr. Brasier worked in a criminal defense firm in Oakland, California before he and his family moved up to Portland. Mr. Brasier now lives in the area, and spends his time working, spending time with his wife and two children, kayaking with his son and involving himself in the community. In addition to his legal work, Mr Brasier works pro bono for low-income children in his spare time. Having done his undergraduate studies in Portland and being a native of the area, Tom has great affection for the city and its people.

Professionally, Mr. Brasier handles all aspects of Family Law cases. While the bulk of this surrounds divorces and child custody, he regularly handles adoptions, child support matters, restraining order and anything else that touches on the legal aspects of domestic relations. He takes an honest approach to complex issues and works hard to find a resolution that suits his client and everyone involved. Since many of the cases Tom deals with have to do with children, he makes great effort to ensure that children's welfare is at the forefront of his priorities.

attorneys.name: Sawyer D. Burton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Sawyer Burton knows that behind every case is a person’s future—and he fights relentlessly to protect it while guiding clients with compassion. At Morris Family Law LLC, Sawyer represents clients in divorce, custody, parenting time, child and spousal support matters, and protective orders. He also brings his extensive criminal defense background to the firm, defending clients facing misdemeanors, felonies, and DUII charges.

A seasoned litigator, Sawyer has built his career in the courtroom, standing up for clients in high-stakes situations. He began at Metropolitan Public Defender, where he earned a reputation for fearless advocacy while defending individuals with mental health challenges and those accused of serious criminal offenses. In private practice, he expanded into civil litigation and family law, blending his sharp trial skills with the understanding and sensitivity that family law clients need most.

Originally from Tucson, Arizona, Sawyer earned his undergraduate degree at Hampshire College and pursued graduate research in Hefei, China, where he studied the effects of pesticides on honey bees and became fluent in Mandarin Chinese. He went on to graduate cum laude from Vermont Law School, where he served on the Law Review.

Now admitted to practice in Oregon, Arizona, and the Federal District of Oregon, Sawyer is known for his clear communication, steady guidance, and unwavering dedication. Whether helping a parent fight for time with their child or defending someone against a life-altering charge, Sawyer’s clients know they have an advocate who will listen, stand with them, and fight tirelessly for their future.

Matt met and married his wife during college and they now have two children. Among other things, he enjoys soccer, rock climbing, waterskiing and the outdoors in general. He also enjoys spending whatever time he can with his wife and kids.

attorneys.name: Brian D. Chenoweth
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Brian formed CLG in 2006, after an 8-year, successful run as the co-founder and managing partner of Rycewicz and Chenoweth, LLP. Brian represents clients in all aspects of commercial litigation in state and federal courts. With over 25 years of experience in law, Brian is recognized for his litigation work with plaintiffs and defendants alike throughout Oregon and Washington.

Practice Areas:

Business: Brian has handled many business disputes in his career, including shareholder disputes, partnership disputes, trade secret litigation, unfair competition, financial fraud, contract disputes, and UCC cases. Having seen how poorly drafted agreements lead to litigation, Brian also enjoys counseling businesses on their business transactions and improving their contracts.

Real Estate: Brian provides deep experience in real estate disputes, including breach of contract, failure to disclose material defects, boundary and easement disputes, and partition actions.

Employment: Brian regularly counsels clients on employment matters and litigates those cases that cannot be resolved informally. Brian represents both employers and employees, including executives in their employment claims. Representing both sides of an area of law allows a lawyer to understand the strategy and thinking of opposing counsel.

Environmental: Brian's environmental clients include property owners and businesses facing regulatory compliance and cleanup costs for all types of contamination. In addition, Brian represents clients in matters regarding environmental consultant and contractor negligence, water quality, wetlands, landslides, and bodily injury and property damage related to chemicals, lead, asbestos and mold.

Insurance: Brian has successfully handled numerous insurance disputes and has represented insurance companies and policy holders. Today he only represents policy holders in insurance coverage disputes for property damage and injury. Brian's expertise is in forcing insurance companies to pay to defend their insureds when they are sued and to pay the cost of settlements or judgments. His work includes general liability policies, errors and omissions/professional negligence policies, directors and officers policies, and first-party property and casualty insurance.

Construction: Brian represents contractors, subcontractors, and owners in all types of construction disputes, including construction defect, construction injury, breach of contract, construction liens, and surety/bond disputes.

Representative clients: Brian enjoys working with a diverse group of clients, large and small, in-state and out-of-state, established companies and start ups. His clients include manufacturers, retailers, food and wine producers, cannabis related business, restaurants, banks and lenders, developers, outdoor advertising companies, construction companies, municipal housing authorities, personal representatives and trustees, trucking companies, environmental consultants and clean-up contractors, testing laboratories, private universities, and individuals, to name a few.

Philosophy: Since founding CLG, Brian's passion has been a mission of never ending improvement on how CLG delivers legal services and creates value for its clients. As Brian explains, "Not having started my career in a large law firm, I look at things differently than most lawyers who did. I am always asking myself whether there is a better, more efficient, way to do something. I instill in our lawyers the values of creative thinking, strategy, and innovation in all that we do. To be successful, you need to be a least three steps ahead of the lawyer on the other side. I am also a champion of plain speak and direct communication, and I actively discourage the use of unnecessary legalese. Lawyers need to communicate with their clients in a way that allows them to understand what is happening in their legal matter without having to consult a law dictionary multiple times."

Licensed to practice law in Oregon and Washington, Brian received his law degree (cum laude) from the American University, Washington College of Law in 1994, and a Bachelors of Arts in political science from the University of Oregon in 1989.

Brian has given lectures to industry professionals, governmental agency staff and other lawyers on environmental, insurance, real estate and land use law.

Away from the office, Brian enjoys seeing and playing music, boating on "Sunshine Daydream", traveling, and spending time with friends and family. He is currently working on one of his bucket list items — to become a competent tennis player.

Arne is currently an active member of the following organizations:

Arne Cherkoss was born and raised in Los Angeles, California. At age sixteen, he relocated to Arcata, California where he graduated from Arcata High School in 1989. That same year, he enrolled at Humboldt State University (also in Arcata). In 1991, Arne transferred to California State University Dominguez Hills, in Southern California. He received a Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies, with Honors, in 1993.

Rather than going directly to graduate school, Arne chose to pursue his dream of being a touring recording artist. From 1994 through 2000, Arne spent his time writing music and playing with his two bands. During that time, he recorded numerous CDs, toured the United States seven times, and went on a six week European tour.

In 2000, Arne was accepted to the University of Oregon School Of Law in Eugene, Oregon. He received his JD in 2003. While attending the U of O, Arne volunteered at Lane County Legal Aid. While there, he represented low income clients in civil disputes. Arne also worked for the University as a Student Defender, representing students in administrative disciplinary hearings. During his last semester of law school, Arne served as a law clerk for Lane County Circuit Court judge, Lyle Velure.

In 2003, Arne was admitted to the Oregon State Bar and was hired by Frohnmayer Deatherage, a premier Southern Oregon law firm. While at Frohnmayer, Arne's practice focused on Insurance Defense, Professional Liability, and Family Law.

In 2007, Arne's friend and law school classmate, Tim Williams, offered him a job and the chance to live in Bend, Oregon. In May 2007, Arne began working with Tim Williams and Roy Dwyer. The focus of his practice is statewide personal injury litigation.

Arne's interests include snowboarding, hiking, biking, reading, playing music and spending time with his wife Laurel (who is also an attorney) and his two Parson Jack Russell Terriers.

attorneys.bio: Tim has been practicing law in the Tri-Cities for more than 20 years, helping business and families achieve success, and plan for their futures. His practice focuses on commerical law, business formation and governance, real estate, estate planning, and family law matters. Tim grew up in Walla Walla, and graduated from Walla Walla High School in 1975. He went on to receive a BA in International Relations from Brigham Young University (1990), and his J.D. from Creighton University (1993). After law school, he joined a local law firm, Leavy Schultz Davis and Fearing, and worked there for three years. He then joined Lamb-Weston, a subsidiary of ConAgra Foods. With Lamb-Weston, Tim not only filled the role of associate general counsel, he also ran sales regions in the Northern California, and Toronto, Canada. He also worked in production, negotiated grower contracts, supplier contracts, handled employment issues, dealt with the Perishable Agricultural Commodity Act, and import/export matters. His experience with Lamb-Weston has given Tim insight and experience in running businesses that allows him to help his clients in all aspects of their business in a practical way. Tim returned to private practice in 2005 with Coke Roth. In 2009, Tim struck out on his own as a sole practitioner. In 2013 Tim joing Olsen Daines as "Of Counsel" in addition to maintaining his own private practice. Tim is married to Kim Coleman, his wife of 21 years. They have four terrific kids, Ty, Michael,, Trey and Sydney. Kim is a citizen of New Zealand, so his children enjoy both U.S. and New Zealand citizenship, with Sydney, who was born while they lived in Canada also enjoying Canadian citizenship. When time from work and family activities allows, Tim enjoys golf, basketball, skiing, reading, and working out. You can often spot him riding his bike to his office and even to court. Please don't run him down, although rumor has it he may be worth more dead than alive (just a joke).

John Coletti grew up in Hillsboro, Oregon, and received his undergraduate degree from the University of Washington in 1991. John earned his law degree from the Willamette University College of Law in 1994 where he served as an associate editor of the Willamette Law Review. John has achieved several million dollar verdicts and settlements on behalf of injured clients, including a jury verdict of 12.1 Million dollars. John is listed as one of the Best Lawyers in America; an Oregon Super Lawyer; and one of Portland's Best Lawyers in Portland Monthly magazine.

John's practice is dedicated to representing injured individuals in cases involving defective products, medical malpractice, negligence, insurance bad faith and maritime, railroad and construction injuries.

John likes to be involved in the community and is involved with the March of Dimes.

attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Eugene, OR
attorneys.bio:
I grew up in Sandy, Oregon, and I am an outdoor enthusiast. I enjoy walking, hiking, biking, jogging and swimming. I was interested in the law as a way to help people with their problems.

I attended Oregon State University and earned my B.S. Degree with a minor in Political Science. I graduated with summa cum laude honors. I worked with Audrey Back at ASOSU student advising office and learned that helping students with their legal issues was challenging, rewarding and never the same issue twice. Everyone had a unique issue that they needed help with.

I graduated from The University of Oregon School of Law in 1998. I clerked at a personal injury law office and learned that I could help one client at a time and make a difference in someone’s life. I found this very rewarding.

I had my son while attending law school. I learned how to balance work and family responsibilities. I offer flexible hours today as a result. I am able to meet clients in the Eugene are for later evening appointments and weekend appointments when necessary.

I charge a reasonable fee for my services. I understand the financial strain most people are experiencing. I have been a single parent and also dealt with student loans and unexpected medical expenses. I know how challenging these issues are.

My goal is to help clients get a fresh start and get ahead of their debts so they can live happy and healthy lives. Families deserve to plan for their own retirement and save for their children’s college education.

attorneys.name: Douglas P. Cushing
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy and Creditors' Rights Lawyers in Grants Pass, OR
attorneys.bio:
Douglas P. Cushing brings 50 years of practical legal knowledge and experience to Cauble, Furr & Beguin, LLP in commercial law and estate planning and probate practice. His background produces a willingness and demonstrates ability to shape options and solutions to complex problems for his clients.

In the estate arena. Doug began practicing the same year the Oregon Probate Code was redrawn. So, his experience has mirrored the implementation of those statutes. He has handled estates of significant size with large estate tax risks, as well as modest estates with contentious heir disputes. that have entailed litigation, mediation, and tax audits. Doug always addresses the "people" issues as well as the financial consequences to his clients. His goal is to achieve his clients' goals, minimizing tax impacts while preserving client privacy. Licensed in both Oregon and Washington. Doug has extensive experience throughout the Pacific Northwest.

On the commercial law side. Doug has not only served on behalf of banks and other lending institutions, but he has handled debtor problems, including complex Chapter 11 cases through to successful plan implementation. That perspective makes him uniquely able to protect creditors rights when analyzing financial disputes from the lender's side. In structuring loan documentation for a lender. he is able to foresee risks to be avoided before his clients have made commitments, they might later regret. In his five decades of practice. Doug has advised both public entities and "mom and pop operators in financing, business sales, and property disputes.

Finding solutions for his clients has always been Doug's primary goal. but outside the law practice, Doug has been a regular participant and board member in local and larger school and civic entities. He enjoys golf, gardening, grandchildren, and everything Stanford.

attorneys.name: Shane Davis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury & Wrongful Death Lawyers in Eugene, OR
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Shane Davis works tirelessly to learn every nuanced detail of a client's case. He works closely with a team of dedicated and skilled legal staff to give his clients the best likelihood of success-both in settlement negotiations and at trial. Licensed to practice in all Oregon state and federal courts, Shane has successfully represented hundreds of clients, achieving justice for those injured in car crashes, pedestrian and cyclist collisions, trucking crashes, premises liability claims, and wrongful death. Shane is experienced in complex civil litigation, handling matters involving medical malpractice, dangerously defective products, and automotive crashworthiness.

A member of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association, the American Association for Justice, and elected by his peers to the Lane County Bar Association Board of Directors, Shane is actively engaged in the Oregon legal community. He serves on the Lane County Law Library Advisory Committee and is a contributing author and editor of the Oregon State Bar Professional Liability Fund's biennial publication entitled Oregon Statutory Time Limitations.

Shane received his law degree from the University of Oregon School of Law, graduating with Pro Bono Honors for his work in the community. In law school, Shane was a member of the Moot Court Board and a two-time national moot court finalist. Prior to joining JJL&M, Shane worked as a law clerk for the Trial Division of the Oregon Department of Justice. He also completed an externship in United States District Court with the Honorable Mustafa T. Kasubhai.

Shane received his Bachelor's degree from the University of Nevada, Reno, dual majoring in economics and political science. Before law school, he worked as a business development analyst for a Nevada-based renewable energy company. Outside of the office, Shane spends his free time running, hiking and, playing chess.

attorneys.bio:
Jason’s practice focuses on complex litigation, including the defense of product liability, toxic tort, environmental and commercial litigation claims. He has diverse trial court experience, having tried cases, mediated or argued dispositive motions in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California courts. In addition to his trial practice, Jason has successfully mediated or arbitrated hundreds of other cases throughout the Pacific Northwest.

Best Lawyers has recognized Jason for inclusion in its Best Lawyers in America list since 2019, including selections for Mass Torts/Class Actions (2019-2024), Product Liability Litigation – Defendants (2024), and Commercial Litigation (2024). Jason serves as national counsel for several product manufacturers and distributors in toxic tort litigation, overseeing strategic planning, discovery, motions practice, expert witness development, settlement negotiations and trial. His experience also includes the representation of agricultural cooperatives, product manufacturers, property owners, lessees, and other commercial entities in pre-suit disputes, along with litigation in state and federal courts.

attorneys.bio:
Melodie brings more than a decade of prosecutorial experience to her work at Gilroy Napoli Short, offering clients a deep understanding of how criminal cases are built and pursued. During her time as a Deputy District Attorney in Marion County, she handled a wide spectrum of matters, ranging from DUII and domestic violence cases to complex financial crimes, major drug prosecutions, firearms offenses, and serious Measure 11 crimes, including homicide. This extensive courtroom background enables Melodie to anticipate challenges, develop strong defense strategies, and advocate effectively for fair and balanced outcomes.

Drawing on her firsthand knowledge of the criminal justice system, Melodie is committed to guiding clients through difficult legal situations with clarity, compassion, and determination. She prioritizes open communication and works closely with each individual to ensure they understand their options and feel supported at every stage of their case.

Melodie earned her undergraduate degree in political science from Oregon State University and received her Juris Doctor from Willamette University College of Law. In addition to her law degree, she completed a Certificate in Dispute Resolution, strengthening her ability to resolve cases efficiently through negotiation and alternative methods when appropriate.

Outside the office, Melodie values time with her husband and children and enjoys exploring new baking projects in her kitchen.

He also developed significant experience working on cases involving individuals with mental health challenges, allowing him to approach sensitive situations with insight, professionalism, and compassion.

Conner’s legal background extends beyond traditional courtroom practice. He previously clerked with the District Attorney’s Offices in Multnomah, Lane, and Jackson Counties and contributed to criminal justice policy while working in the Oregon State Legislature as a criminal law advisor. This combination of prosecutorial, legislative, and clerking experience gives him a well-rounded perspective on how criminal laws are created, enforced, and applied.

Drawing on this diverse experience, Conner is committed to guiding clients through difficult and often overwhelming circumstances. He prioritizes clear communication and works diligently to pursue outcomes that are fair, balanced, and aligned with his clients’ best interests.

Conner earned his undergraduate degree in Political Science and Religious Studies from the University of Oregon and completed his legal education at the University of Oregon School of Law. A native of Medford, Oregon, and the son of two educators, he brings strong values and a grounded approach to his work. Outside the office, Conner enjoys spending time with his family and keeping up with his energetic children.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Elliott
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Tualatin, OR
attorneys.bio:
For me, the law has become an integral part of my life. It’s where I find my meaning as a man, a husband, a father, and a lawyer. When people ask me what kind of lawyer I am, I usually tell them that first and foremost, I am a peacemaker.

My path to a career in law began with earning a B.S. degree at Portland State University. A law professor there steered me to Willamette University, where I earned my JD in 1984. Thus far, I’ve been living the American Dream. I’ve been married for over 40 years and have two children and four grandchildren.

I’ve been practicing law in Tualatin now for well over 40 years. In that time, I’ve represented many people with a lot of different people problems. I’ve learned what it means to help with suffering the law’s sting, in all its many legal forms. I have purposely chosen not to specialize in any one area of law because I’ve learned that a good dose of common sense is usually sufficient to solve most legal problems. For these reasons, I have chosen to be a general practitioner. I help people with what I can, and if I cannot help them, I refer them to a specialist when one is truly needed.

If you are suffering from a legal hurt, let me try to get you back on track to the life you want.

attorneys.name: Chance Fewel
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
“Chance is the type of attorney who immediately rolls up his sleeves and gets his hands dirty”, notes Managing Attorney Colin Amos. “He is not afraid to take on the most complicated case and follow it through to conclusion. This is why he has had such success in child custody cases which are often the most contentious types of cases in family law.” Having litigated numerous Trials gives him a decisive advantage in both negotiations and trial if necessary. His clients appreciate his compassionate, direct and decisive advice when making tough decisions. “Once a decision has been made, his clients take comfort in knowing they have an attorney that will follow through.”

Chance gets that family law is about helping people when they need help. He further notes that “there is nothing more important than your children and their safety. “I have the ability to provide outstanding personal and professional support during this highly emotional process. I have the experience to take cases the distance to trial, but am progressive enough to take advantage of alternative dispute resolution methods such as Mediation.”

attorneys.name: Sonya Fischer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lake Oswego, OR
attorneys.bio:
Sonya Fischer has extensive experience as an advocate for vulnerable populations. Her activism stems from parenting a child with severe developmental disabilities. The institutional barriers that she experienced as a young mother inspired her to speak up and create change for those in need of human services.

While attending Warner Pacific College, Sonya organized parents of children with disabilities to secure important early intervention services. She was soon recruited by Multnomah County, where she assisted the families of children with disabilities in accessing services and facilitated the planning and delivery of services for early childhood education, domestic violence and homeless youth.

In 1991, while completing her master's degree in Public Administration at Portland State University, Sonya began working as an intern for the late senator Frank Roberts, where she spearheaded new disability parking permit legislation. Sonya worked in Salem for 13 years. While working with the Oregon Council on Developmental Disabilities, Sonya helped create a system of in-home supports for children with severe disabilities and facilitated the passage of legislation making it possible for children with disabilities to continue attending the same school when living temporarily outside their parents' home. As legislative staff to Senator Frank Shields, Sonya developed a package of early childhood legislation that resulted in a statewide childcare provider training program that incorporated the importance of healthy brain development for young children.

Sonya graduated from the Lewis & Clark Law School, where she was recognized for her leadership and contributions as both a Joyce Ann Harpole Scholar and a member of the Cornelius Honor Society. The Harpole award is a peer-nominated award given each year to a law student and a practicing lawyer who are notable for balancing a fulfilling life with the study or practice of law. Sonya was also recognized for winning the mock trial competition. While in law school, Sonya spearheaded a pro bono program for law students to assist families with their children's special education planning.

Sonya is a member of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association, where she co-chairs the New Lawyers Section. She is also involved with Oregon Women Lawyers, The Arc of Multnomah County, and the Families and Advocates Coalition. She is active in her children's education, previously serving on school foundation boards and budget committees as well as volunteering in the classroom.

Sonya is a frequent presenter at conferences on topics ranging from family issues to community organizing and effective legislative advocacy.

A member of the Oregon State Bar since 2003, Sonya brings compassion and first-hand legislative knowledge to the practice of law. She combines her legal expertise with her understanding of education and service delivery systems to create successful strategies for her clients. Sonya understands her clients' struggles and utilizes a collaborative approach while building a solid record to preserve her clients' rights.

attorneys.name: Ashley R. Fraley
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support & Custody & Parenting Time Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Ashley Fraley is a dedicated professional who is passionate about assisting families during challenging times. With a genuine commitment to helping clients regain control in their lives, Ashley understands the importance of patiently explaining complex processes in a way that individuals can truly comprehend. By providing clear explanations, Ashley empowers clients with knowledge, enabling them to make informed decisions during periods of uncertainty.

In her work, Ashley demonstrates diligence in understanding her clients' goals and aspirations. She prioritizes transparency and honesty, ensuring that clients have a realistic understanding of what can be achieved based on their specific circumstances. By setting clear expectations and offering practical advice, Ashley helps clients navigate their legal matters with a sense of confidence and purpose.

One of Ashley's core beliefs is that it's perfectly acceptable not to have all the answers, as long as one knows how to find them. She embraces a continuous learning mindset and is always ready to seek out the necessary information to best serve her clients. Ashley understands that every individual's journey is unique, and she encourages her clients to focus on their own progress rather than comparing themselves to others. This mindset fosters a supportive and empathetic environment where clients can feel understood and respected.

Guiding someone through a difficult period requires a delicate balance of patience and honesty. Ashley values the opportunity to support her clients during their lowest points, providing them with the guidance and reassurance they need to move forward. Whether it's navigating the aftermath of a divorce or assisting with modifications, Ashley believes in equipping her clients with the knowledge and understanding of their options. By doing so, she helps restore a sense of power and control to individuals who may feel overwhelmed by the dissolution process.

When not advocating for her clients, Ashley enjoys EDM music festivals and spending time with her dogs Madeye (Saint Bernard) and Dobby (Corgi).

attorneys.name: Deanna L. Franco
attorneys.practice_type: Estate & Trust Planning Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Deanna is an experienced attorney providing advice and counsel to clients in the areas of: estate and tax planning, probate and trust administration (including tax compliance), guardianship and conservatorship matters, entity formation, governance and general business planning, as well as associated commercial and residential real estate transactions. Her clients range from individuals with modest to high-net worth estates, corporations to family-owned businesses, as well as fiduciaries and beneficiaries.

Creative problem solving is one of the most rewarding parts of Deanna’s practice. She collaborates with clients and their advisors to implement solutions tailored to address their specific unique goals and needs. Deanna enjoys getting to know her clients and takes immense pride in being able to assist them through the various stages of their personal and/or business lives. Deanna’s compassionate and detailed approach to the practice of law brings her clients piece of mind in what may be emotional and stressful events.

Having worked at the Marion County District Attorney’s Office and in a general practice firm prior to joining Cosgrave Vergeer Kester LLP, Deanna has a broad ranging background in a number of practice areas in addition to her current practice, including family law and general litigation.

attorneys.name: Aaron D. Frishman
attorneys.practice_type: Asset Protection Planning Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
With almost 20 years of experience in estate planning, Aaron has learned one fundamental truth – estate planning is a highly personal, and in many cases, emotional endeavor for individuals and their families. Aaron appreciates this fact, and treats every relationship with his clients as just that, a meaningful relationship. He has learned that every person’s plan, while in some cases may be similar to others, is unique in and of itself and always requires special attention to details. Whether it is from generating a more “basic” plan for younger families with children, to developing more sophisticated tax plans for high-net-worth clients, Aaron’s ultimate goal is to assist all clients, regardless of asset level and wealth, to enable them to protect their assets for themselves, their families, and their loved ones, while minimizing tax liability and exposure. When families lose a loved one, Aaron also works closely with fiduciaries and beneficiaries to help them navigate probate, estate, and trust administration, to ensure that proper wishes are met and that tax matters are sufficiently addressed.

Aaron feels fortunate to be able to incorporate his experience practicing in Elder Law with his planning. He is able to identify and plan for important issues, that may not have been previously seen, related to long-term healthcare costs, special needs planning, and issues related to public benefits. On a more general level, Aaron helps and directs clients who may own or run businesses and not-for-profits and assists with general corporate matters related to corporate entity creation, corporate governance, business succession planning, and liability and privacy matters.

Aaron is licensed to practice in Oregon, Washington, New York, and Colorado. He has lectured to a diverse range of individuals and professionals in multiple states on various topics including estate and tax planning, planning for incapacity, trust administration, and special needs trusts. Aaron lives in West Linn, Oregon with his wife, son, and “BoJack” (Boston Terrier/Jack Russell mix). When not assisting clients, he enjoys experiencing anything outdoors in the PNW, playing sports – softball and volleyball, skiing in the winter, and rooting on his teenage son, Jack who has become quite a competitive baseball player.

With an MBA and a stint at one of the country's largest accounting firms, Zach is equally comfortable in matters of both law and business. attorneys.name: Michael Fuller
attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
I escaped the trailer park in pursuit of the American Dream. Now I’m a partner at Olsen Daines PC and a professor at Lewis & Clark Law School. My rate is $410 per hour. About 20% of my cases are pro bono at no charge. As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a lawyer. Growing up poor in Hillsboro, we didn’t know any lawyers. My inspiration to practice law came from TV shows and movies. I watched street-smart attorneys fight for underdogs, regardless of their ability to pay. Last year I was ranked among the top 2.5% of my peers by Super Lawyers magazine. My Martindale-Hubbell AV rating is Preeminent. I’m the Oregon State Bar consumer section past chair, Oregon Trial Lawyers Association consumer section past chair, and National Association of Consumer Advocates Oregon Chapter past chair. The day I passed the bar was the best day in my life. I was held back in the first grade and expelled from middle school. Read my old report card. I come from humble beginnings, was raised in a trailer park by a single mom, and am the first in my family to attend college. Now I dedicate about 20% of my practice to pro bono. I’m honored to chair my firm’s consumer protection group. Olsen Daines is one of the largest consumer bankruptcy law firms in the Northwest. Our attorneys have helped over 30,000 consumers since 1978.

attorneys.practice_type: DUI/DWI Lawyers in Beaverton, OR

Shelley has lived in the Pacific Northwest for the last fifteen years and loves it here. Although she calls Oregon home, she remains and avid and loyal Green Bay Packer fan. attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Grants Pass, OR
attorneys.bio: Kellie A. Furr was born in England and later spent her childhood in the low country of South Carolina. She then attended a small liberal arts college, College of Charleston. After spending a couple of years working as an environmental consultant in Charleston, Kellie attended University of South Carolina School of Law and Vermont Law School in a dual-degree J.D./Masters of Environmental Law and Policy Program. Right after graduation, Kellie journeyed out West with her beloved dog, Woody. Kellie carved out her own personal injury litigation practice in the Portland metro prior to joining forces with Cauble, Furr & Beguin, LLP. Kellie practices in several areas of civil litigation, including personal injury, civil rights, contract disputes, elder abuse, and child sexual abuse. In her spare time, Kellie enjoys competitive power lifting, creating fine art, gardening, and playing the tin whistle very, very badly.

attorneys.name: Kevin C. Gage
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Salem, OR
attorneys.bio:
Kevin C. Gage grew up in Washington. He excelled in college attending first Washington State University and then the University of Washington where he graduated Phi Beta Kappa with a B.A. in Classical Greek.

Mr. Gage received his J.D. degree from Willamette University Law School in 1981. In that same year he entered private practice, working for a firm that specialized in Divorce and Family Law. In 1984, Mr. Gage began the solo practice of law, limiting his practice exclusively to Family Law.

Mr. Gage is co-author of "Property Rights and Division," chapter 6 of the Oregon State Bar Publication "Dissolution Practice." He has authored other articles relating to Domestic Relations topics and has served as a speaker at Domestic Relations conferences.

Mr. Gage is a member of the Marion County Bar Association and a member of the Domestic Relations Section of the Oregon State Bar. As a member of the Domestic Relations Section, Mr. Gage has served on the Executive Committee and on the Legislation Committee.

Serving as an Arbitrator in domestic relations cases is a part of Mr. Gage's practice.

attorneys.name: Brad Gerke
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
“Divorce, custody and modification proceedings have far more to do with strategy than drafting or filing documents” states managing attorney Colin Amos. “Brad’s background as a former professional poker player gives him a decisive advantage in the practice of family law. Any attorney can prepare general documents but when your relationship with your children or financial future is on the line it is comforting to have a passionate strategist.”

“You have to be willing to change gears in any case,” says Brad. “Each case requires a different approach, and during a case, as the case changes, so should your approach. I try to create game plans with clients that address their needs. There are certainly cases where the best results will come by being aggressive early, but there are other cases where finesse is a better route - the key is in knowing the difference.”

Brad is experienced in all phases of litigation including Depositions, negotiation and Trial. Prior experience as a City Prosecutor has assisted Brad in an extensive understanding of FAPA cases.

attorneys.name: John Gilroy
attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
John Gilroy is a founding partner of Gilroy Napoli Short, LLC, where he represents individuals facing serious criminal charges, DUI offenses, and personal injury claims throughout Oregon. With extensive courtroom experience and a background in prosecution, John brings strategic insight and trial-tested advocacy to every case he handles.

Before co-founding the firm, John served as a Deputy District Attorney with the Washington County District Attorney’s Office, one of the largest and most active prosecutor’s offices in the state. In that role, he handled a broad spectrum of cases, including misdemeanors, DUII offenses, and major felony prosecutions. His firsthand experience evaluating evidence, preparing cases for trial, and negotiating resolutions on behalf of the state gives him a unique advantage when defending clients in criminal court. Today, he leverages that prosecutorial background to anticipate the strategies of the opposing side and build strong, results-driven defense strategies.

John’s legal skill and commitment to client advocacy have earned him consistent professional recognition. He has been selected as an Oregon Super Lawyer for five consecutive years, a distinction awarded to attorneys who demonstrate a high degree of peer recognition and professional achievement. In 2014, he was also invited to join The National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers, an honor reserved for attorneys who exhibit superior qualifications, trial results, and leadership in the legal community. These distinctions reflect his reputation for excellence in criminal defense litigation and trial advocacy.

Education and Early Career

John received his Bachelor’s Degree in Political Science from Santa Clara University in 1993. He later earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Oregon School of Law in 1998. Prior to attending law school, he worked in Washington, D.C. as a legislative aide for Robert Packwood, gaining valuable experience in government and public policy.

Deep Oregon Roots

Born and raised in the Portland metropolitan area, John comes from a family with a strong legal tradition. He is the son of the late Patrick D. Gilroy, who served as a respected judge on the Clackamas County Circuit Court. Growing up in a household grounded in public service and the rule of law influenced John’s commitment to justice and ethical advocacy. Two of his brothers also practice law in the Portland metro area, continuing the family’s longstanding involvement in the Oregon legal community.

Commitment Beyond the Courtroom

Outside of his practice, John prioritizes time with his wife and five children. He enjoys golf, skiing, and fishing, as well as basketball, hiking, and camping throughout the Pacific Northwest. His connection to the local community strengthens his dedication to protecting the rights and futures of the individuals and families he represents.

attorneys.name: Daniel T. Goldstein
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in West Linn, OR
attorneys.bio:
Dan Goldstein has earned a reputation as a successful trial lawyer specializing in construction and real estate litigation, routinely representing owners, contractors, and design professionals in claims regarding defect, delay, non-payment, non-disclosure, breach of contract, boundary disputes, and easement disputes.

Over the last 18 years, Dan has tried nearly 50 cases to juries, judges, and arbitrators, achieving awards ranging in size from $20,000 to $5,000,000. Leveraging this experience, Dan has also achieved favorable settlements for his clients in hundreds of other matters.

Dan is rated AV-Preeminent with Martindale-Hubbell, has been listed in Best Lawyers in America for construction litigation in the Portland market since 2013, and has been listed in Oregon Super Lawyers in the area of Construction Litigation since 2016. Dan attended law school at the University of Washington after obtaining his undergraduate degree from Portland State University.

In addition to litigating complex construction cases, Dan has helped shape important points of law in Oregon, having successfully briefed and argued several key cases of complex construction issues before the Oregon Supreme Court and the Oregon Court of Appeals, including the following:

• PIH Beaverton, LLC v. Super One, Inc.

• Sunset Presbyterian Church v. Brockamp and Jaeger, Inc.

• Shell v. The Schollander Companies, Inc.

• Wood Park Terrace Apartment LP v. Tri-Vest, LLC

• Sunset Presbyterian Church v. Andersen Construction Co.

Outside of the office, Dan plays trumpet in local venues and teaches trumpet lessons on a limited basis. Dan also plays tournament racquetball locally and enjoys outdoor activities such as biking and running. Dan and his wife volunteer with the Clackamas County 4-H Camp throughout the year.

Clients, colleagues, and judges have said the following about Dan:

"The best civil attorney I've had in my courtroom, bar none."

- Circuit Court Judge

"Dan is a terrific lawyer; he is incredibly knowledgeable, is a skilled strategist, and has the personal skills to make you feel at ease throughout the whole process. Dan helped myself and 18 other homeowners in a construction defect litigation. Thanks to his expertise and tenacity we received the best outcome possible. Dan's guidance, knowledge, communication and personable nature made everyone feel confident we were in great hands."

- Client

"Excellent construction defect plaintiff counsel. A fierce advocate with high ethical standards, while we are frequently adversaries he had my utmost respect."

- Attorney

"We were about to walk away from a real-estate deal going awry when we decided to consult Dan. Not only did he help us understand our rights, but he also set the other party straight when no one else could. He speaks so logically and respectfully that he got the other party to acquiesce easily."

- Client

"Dan was professional, approachable, practical and always accessible (responded personally to an email from me at an unreasonable hour). Dan worked diligently to understand the moving parts that made our case viable. Dan contacted our expert witness on several occasions to verify details, confirm understandings and narrow down ambiguity. Ultimately we ended with the most favorable result possible."

-Client

attorneys.name: C.J. Graves
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
C.J. invests himself in each and every case he handles, and has a passion for helping his clients resolve their legal matters and move forward with their lives. He has spent his career as a litigator and a trial attorney, and is more comfortable in a court room than in an office.

In addition to his family law work, C.J. has handled matters involving torts from employment discrimination, to traffic accidents, to sexual assault, to wrongful death cases. He has a passion for helping individuals and for helping give voice to the individual stories of each of his clients. He served as first chair in numerous trials, including high-conflict cases relating to dissolution, domestic violence, parenting time, custody, and division of property. He has handled legal issues involving jurisdictional challenges, high asset dissolutions, tax implications, and complex matters involving marital estate finance, including but not limited to the separation of businesses, retirement accounts, pensions, and spousal support.

Although C.J. is proficient in the courtroom, he always seeks to resolve cases in the manner most expedient and beneficial to his client's interests. C.J. carefully listens to each of his client's concerns and desires, and tailors the outcomes to suit the client's individualized needs. As a result, C.J. has had remarkable success settling cases for clients, and crafting equitable remedies fit for the specific client.

Prior to law school, C.J. conducted research on juror decision-making, and gave a presentation on the topic at a conference for academic psychologists. He also worked as a jury consultant and psychological analyst on several tort cases. At least two of these cases resulted in multi-million dollar verdicts.
