attorneys.name: Jennifer J. Middleton
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Eugene, OR
attorneys.bio:
Shareholder Jennifer Middleton brings twenty-five years of distinctive legal service, advancing and defending the rights of individuals in employment and civil rights matters including constitutional claims, discrimination, Title IX, whistleblowing, False Claims Act, sexual harassment, disability rights, and medical leave.

Jennifer represents employees and individuals in discrimination and civil rights claims against employers, schools, and governments. She was co-lead counsel on the 2014 case winning the right to marry for same-sex couples in Oregon. In Jane Doe v. The University of Oregon, she represented the student who reported a gang rape by three members of the Ducks basketball team, pursuing Title IX claims against the University for its inadequate response. She has represented victims of abuse at the hands of police, jails, and prisons; female athletes in securing equal treatment by their schools; and transgender people seeking equal access to health care and jobs.

Jennifer maintains an active practice representing whistleblowers, assisting them to report wrongdoing and responding to any retaliation they may experience. This includes claims under the federal False Claims Act ("qui tam" cases) and other statutes providing incentives for whistleblowers to report illegal activities. Jennifer strives not only to secure fair compensation for her clients but also to maintain high ethical and legal standards in the workplace, schools, and public entities.

Prior to joining Johnson Johnson Lucas & Middleton, Jennifer served as a public interest lawyer with the Employment Law Center in San Francisco and later as a staff attorney with the American Civil Liberties Union at its New York headquarters, prosecuting civil rights claims nationwide. She has authored numerous amicus briefs before the U.S. Supreme Court and has represented individuals in groundbreaking claims. In 2002, for example, Jennifer represented the surviving same-sex partner of a victim of the September 11, 2001 World Trade Center attack and forced the federal government to grant formal recognition to a same-sex relationship for the first time ever. After her public interest career, Jennifer became a partner in the boutique labor and employment firm Levy, Ratner in New York before making a lifestyle choice to move to Eugene.

Jennifer is licensed to practice in federal and state court in Oregon, California and New York, the Second and Ninth Circuit Courts of Appeal, and the United States Supreme Court. She is a past President of Oregon's ACLU Board of Directors. She has also served on the District of Oregon's Federal Local Rules Committee, the Executive Board of the Oregon State Bar's Constitutional Law Committee, and as a Lawyer Representative to the Ninth Circuit Judicial Conference.

The Oregon Women's Lawyer Association nominated her in 2017 for the Federal Bar Association's Sarah Hughes Award, recognizing her work advancing civil and human rights. In 2014, she won the Fighting Spirit Award from Basic Rights Oregon as well as the American Immigration Lawyers Association's Outstanding Leadership for Civil Rights Award.

Jennifer received her Bachelor's Degree from Yale University (Summa Cum Laude) and her J.D. from Harvard Law School (Magna Cum Laude), where she was Editor in Chief of the Harvard Women's Law Journal.

In 2002, for example, Jennifer represented the surviving same-sex partner of a victim of the September 11, 2001 World Trade Center attack and forced the federal government to grant formal recognition to a same-sex relationship for the first time ever. After her public interest career, Jennifer became a partner in the boutique labor and employment firm Levy, Ratner in New York before making a lifestyle choice to move to Eugene.

Jennifer is licensed to practice in federal and state court in Oregon, California and New York, the Second and Ninth Circuit Courts of Appeal, and the United States Supreme Court. She is a past President of Oregon's ACLU Board of Directors. She has also served on the District of Oregon's Federal Local Rules Committee, the Executive Board of the Oregon State Bar's Constitutional Law Committee, and as a Lawyer Representative to the Ninth Circuit Judicial Conference.

The Oregon Women's Lawyer Association nominated her in 2017 for the Federal Bar Association's Sarah Hughes Award, recognizing her work advancing civil and human rights. In 2014, she won the Fighting Spirit Award from Basic Rights Oregon as well as the American Immigration Lawyers Association's Outstanding Leadership for Civil Rights Award.

Jennifer received her Bachelor's Degree from Yale University (Summa Cum Laude) and her J.D. from Harvard Law School (Magna Cum Laude), where she was Editor in Chief of the Harvard Women's Law Journal.

attorneys.name: Joseph Morones
attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Salem, OR
attorneys.bio:
Joseph’s path to criminal defense was shaped early in his legal career through extensive, hands-on courtroom experience. While completing his law degree, he served as a certified law clerk at Gilroy Napoli Short, where he worked on cases throughout Oregon and gained practical insight into courtroom procedures, trial strategy, and client advocacy. This early exposure allowed him to develop a strong foundation in criminal law and a detailed understanding of how the justice system operates.

Joseph further strengthened his legal skills through his clerkship with the Clark County District Attorney’s Office, where he refined his analytical abilities and gained valuable perspective on case evaluation and prosecution strategies. This balanced experience enables him to anticipate challenges and craft thoughtful, effective defense approaches for his clients.

In his practice as a criminal defense attorney, Joseph is deeply committed to protecting his clients’ rights and ensuring they are heard at every stage of the legal process. He places a high value on open, honest communication and works hard to build strong attorney-client relationships based on trust and transparency. Known for his meticulous preparation and determined advocacy, Joseph approaches each case with focus, integrity, and a genuine commitment to justice.

Joseph earned his bachelor’s degree in Government with an emphasis in Legal Studies from Grand Canyon University and received his Juris Doctor from Willamette University College of Law.

Outside the office, Joseph maintains an active lifestyle and enjoys training for triathlons, playing basketball, and spending time with his wife and their goldendoodle.

attorneys.name: Erin K. Morris
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
As the founding partner of Morris Family Law, Erin has built a distinguished career as a family law attorney, driven by empathy, strategic insight, and an unbending commitment to supporting clients and families in legal disputes. A native Oregonian, Erin was born in Newberg and raised in Portland, attending high school at St. Mary’s Academy in the heart of downtown.

Erin’s academic journey reflects her passion for justice and the complexity of the human experience. She completed undergraduate studies in Political Science and Middle East Foreign Policy at American University in Washington, DC, and also spent time at University College Dublin in Ireland, where she studied European Foreign Policy and early Irish legal systems. Erin graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of San Francisco. She later earned her Juris Doctorate from Willamette University College of Law, solidifying her path in family law.

Before opening her own practice in 2020, Erin spent the first eight years of her career working and training alongside some of the most prominent and respected Oregon family law firms in the Portland legal community. This experience allowed her to hone her litigation skills and deepen her understanding of complex family law matters, preparing her to launch her own firm dedicated to providing compassionate and strategic representation for each of her clients and their families.

Erin comes from a family of public servants. Her father, a lifelong public school teacher and state-champion football coach, and her mother, who worked her entire career in local community colleges in Oregon, instilled in her a deep sense of community service, equity, and humanity. These values inspire Erin's dedication to helping families navigate difficult transitions with care, integrity, and deep empathy.

Married to a prominent civil rights attorney in Portland, Oregon, Erin is deeply connected to the legal community. Together, they share a commitment to advocating for justice and equity. They are raising their two young children in the same community where Erin grew up, spending their free time exploring Oregon’s mountains and coastlines. Erin’s experience as a mother informs her empathetic approach to family law, ensuring that the needs and well-being of her clients’ families are always at the forefront of her strategy.

Recognized for her exceptional skills as a trial lawyer and formidable presence in the courtroom, Erin's proficiency extends beyond the courthouse. Erin is skilled in pre-trial litigation strategies, where her innovative and thoughtful approach to resolving high-conflict cases shines. Erin's dedication to seeking amicable and effective resolutions outside of court has earned her a reputation as a problem-solver, adept at navigating the complexities of family law with a focus on preserving the integrity and well-being of the family system and promoting the long-term goals and interests of her clients.

Erin's commitment to her clients and success in the courtroom have been consistently recognized by her peers, as evidenced by her many accolades, including her recognition as an Oregon Family Law “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers Magazine for eight consecutive years (2017 - 2024).

attorneys.name: Matthew R. Muenzen
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support & Custody & Parenting Time Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
I am an experienced and dedicated attorney with a demonstrated history of working in family law, juvenile law, and child welfare law. My career has been driven by a passion for helping others, a value I developed during my time as a police officer and public defense attorney. With a Doctor of Law (JD), Master of Arts (MA), and a Bachelor of Science (BS), I combine a strong legal foundation with hands-on experience to guide, educate, and advocate for my clients.

Since 2008, I have specialized in family law with an emphasis on juvenile law, practicing first in Tennessee and now in Oregon. Over the years, I have represented children and parents in child welfare cases and presented on topics such as child abuse and neglect. I also have extensive experience navigating the challenges of working with the Oregon Department of Human Services, ensuring my clients receive compassionate, personalized, and tenacious representation.

I tailor my approach to each client’s unique needs, whether as a zealous advocate in the courtroom or a collaborative problem-solver seeking resolution. I understand the complexities of family and juvenile law and am committed to providing customized legal advice with respect and compassion. Whether crafting parenting time agreements or handling complex custody disputes, I am dedicated to securing the best possible outcomes for my clients and their families.

When I’m not in the courtroom, I enjoy spending time with my wife and two daughters, exploring Oregon’s natural beauty, discovering new bourbons and coffee blends, working in my yard, quoting my favorite movies, and staying active through strength training.

attorneys.name: Jeff S. Napoli
attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Napoli is a co-founding attorney of Gilroy Napoli Short, LLC, where he represents clients in employment law disputes and serious personal injury litigation throughout Oregon. Before entering private practice, he served as a Deputy District Attorney with the Washington County District Attorney’s Office, trying more than 50 jury trials. That extensive courtroom experience shapes his litigation strategy today—he prepares every case for trial, positioning his clients for maximum leverage in settlement negotiations or in front of a jury.

Jeff’s employment law practice focuses on wrongful termination, workplace discrimination, sexual harassment, racial harassment, retaliation, and whistleblower claims. In addition, he handles high-value tort cases involving auto accidents, bicycle accidents, premises liability, catastrophic injuries, and wrongful death. Over the past year and a half, he has recovered more than $2.5 million for his clients, reflecting his commitment to securing full compensation for lost wages, medical expenses, and pain and suffering.

Jeff is admitted to practice in all Oregon state courts and the United States District Court for the District of Oregon. He is a member of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association and several local bar associations. He earned his Juris Doctor from Gonzaga University School of Law, graduating at the top of his class, and his undergraduate degree from Willamette University, where he majored in Psychology and minored in Speech Communication.

Phil is a founding partner of Slinde Nelson. He's a Portland business dispute attorney who practices in a way that is quite distinct from many of his colleagues. In fact, he left big firm practice to offer his clients a different type of service. Phil uses business litigation to drive business solutions, not to churn billable hours, and he frequently advises business clients on proactive litigation avoidance. attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury & Property Damage Liability Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Nicole has defended individuals and businesses in a wide variety of complex litigation matters over her 22-year legal career, including trucking and automobile liability, liquor liability, legal malpractice, and hospitality and hotel-related claims. She is a strong advocate for her clients and an experienced and effective trial/arbitration attorney. Nicole is often retained to defend cases which are of a sensitive nature, such as defending businesses in vicarious liability claims involving sexual assaults by employees and agents.

In addition to her tort/casualty litigation practice, she also specializes in insurance coverage matters and routinely counsels and represents insurance companies regarding disputed claims, coverage lawsuits, and the drafting of policy language.

Nicole also serves as an arbitrator in court-annexed arbitration cases for Multnomah and Washington Counties and on underinsured and uninsured motorist arbitration panels.

Nicole began her legal career in Los Angeles working as an associate in a large health care law firm. She defended doctors and hospitals in medical malpractice claims, with a special emphasis in defending birth injury suits.

attorneys.name: Erin A. O'Riley
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support & Custody & Parenting Time Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
The essence of what I do is to provide advice and advocacy for clients during some of the toughest moments in their lives. My greatest strength in this profession is my ability to listen, empathize, and offer creative solutions to help my clients not only succeed in court but also find a way forward after their family law case concludes. If you were to ask people who know me to describe me in a few words, I believe they would say "thoughtful."

Throughout my career, I've learned that family law is not just about having the best legal arguments; it's about empathy, problem-solving, common sense, and good judgment. These qualities are crucial in achieving positive results when dealing with such personal and sensitive matters. What I like most about helping my clients is calming their fears about the court system, providing them with guidance and support during difficult times.

In my free time, my top three hobbies and passions include working out to stay active and healthy, reading to broaden my horizons, and cooking to experiment with new flavors and cuisines.

attorneys.name: Gregory P. Oliveros
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Clackamas, OR
attorneys.bio:
Greg Oliveros' working style can be summed up in two words: energy and vision. If you have ever met with Greg, you already understand the energy part of the equation. He overflows with enthusiasm and ideas and believes that no matter what, things cannot happen without the big push. His "can do" attitude reflects his philosophy that goals, objectives and outcomes cannot possibly take place without a belief that he can get his clients to that end point. From an outsider's perspective, Greg's vision seems impossible. Greg is constantly thinking about how to serve his clients better and solve his clients' big headaches.

The Oliveros Law Group PC reputation is well known throughout the Portland area as providing high quality legal services to individuals in need.

Greg graduated from Western Oregon College in 1973, earning a Bachelor's Degree in Education. He worked in the Portland Public School District from 1973 to 1987. In the last five years of his career with the Portland Public School District, he was an assistant principal at Humboldt Elementary. Greg also holds two Master’s Degrees from Portland State University, also in Education. For over ten years, Greg was employed as a part time sales person at Nordstrom at Lloyd Center. Greg graduated from Lewis & Clark Law School in 1990 and began practicing law in 1991.

Greg has been actively working as a criminal defense lawyer for over twelve years. His criminal defense practice has emerged as a primary practice area for the firm. Over the same time period, Greg has developed an active civil litigation practice. He and his practice group continue their work in the family law area. Greg is on the Board of Directors of the Family Law Section of the Oregon State Bar.

Greg believes that the Oliveros Law Group PC is committed to excellence and is constantly striving to achieve the best outcomes for all of its clients.

Greg's commitment to the community has involved board memberships and ongoing use of his time and money to support miscellaneous community groups.

Greg is married and has three children and three granddaughters. His daughter, Louren Oliveros, is an accomplished lawyer in New Mexico. Greg and his wife, Gina, are empty nesters and are enjoying the luxury of doing whatever they want, whenever they want.

attorneys.name: Daniel K Olsen
attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bend, OR
attorneys.bio:
Dan is a dedicated criminal defense attorney who provides strong, strategic representation to individuals facing serious charges. With extensive trial experience, he has defended clients in cases ranging from DUII offenses to complex felony and Measure 11 matters. Dan’s practice is built on careful listening, detailed case analysis, and customized defense planning. Whether seeking dismissal, negotiating favorable resolutions, or advocating in the courtroom, he remains focused on protecting his clients’ rights and futures.

Dan’s legal career has been shaped by years of hands-on courtroom work. He has spent more than three years representing clients in criminal defense matters involving everything from misdemeanors to homicide cases. Prior to shifting to defense work, he served as a Deputy District Attorney in Marion County, where he prosecuted property crimes, drug offenses, DUIIs, and serious person crimes under Measure 11. Earlier in his career, Dan practiced family law, handling divorce, custody, and child support matters, and later clerked for a Superior Court Judge in Anchorage, Alaska. He was admitted to the Alaska Bar in 2017 and the Oregon Bar in 2019.

Dan earned his bachelor’s degree in Political Science from Whitworth University in Spokane, where he also competed as a collegiate baseball player. He went on to receive his Juris Doctor from Willamette University College of Law and remained actively involved in legal scholarship and advocacy. During law school, he served as Editor-in-Chief of Willamette Law Online, worked as an editor for the Willamette Journal of International Law and Dispute Resolution, and competed in Moot Court. He is a member of the Marion and Deschutes County Bar Associations and the Oregon Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

Outside of his legal practice, Dan values time with his wife and daughter and enjoys a variety of outdoor activities, including hiking, golfing, hunting, and fishing. He is also a devoted fan of the Seattle Seahawks and Mariners and has a strong interest in the relationship between sports and law. This passion led him to launch a podcast that explores topics ranging from professional athletics to U.S. Supreme Court decisions.

With his broad legal background, trial experience, and client-first approach, Dan brings persistence, skill, and integrity to every case he handles.

attorneys.name: Lars H. Olsen
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio: Lars H. Olsen, managing partner of OlsenDaines P.C., has been a consumer bankruptcy attorney since 1991. With offices throughout the State of Oregon he has helped over ten thousand Oregonians receive a fresh start through the bankruptcy process. Mr. Olsen was raised in Salem, Oregon and graduated from Willamette university in 1988 with a B.S. in American Studies and a minor in Economics. Mr. Olsen graduated from Willamette University College of Law in 1991, having clerked for the Oregon Department of Justice for two years. A tireless advocate for the underdog, Mr. Olsen enjoys assisting those in financial distress receive a "fresh start" and easing the crushing burdens that debts and creditors cause to individuals and families. Mr. Olsen has travelled the state of Oregon from one end to another over the years as an experienced bankruptcy attorney and also for his love for the natural beauty of the State. As a Boy Scout leader and father of four, Mr. Olsen has enjoyed crabbing on the Oregon coast, waterfowl and big game hunting and backpacking in the Oregon wilderness. "Both of my parents were raised in rural Albany during the Great Depression", Mr. Olsen states, "they thaught me at an early age that bad things happen to good people, and we need to help each other along the way."

attorneys.name: Jane Paulson
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Lake Oswego, OR
attorneys.bio:
Jane Paulson is a 1990 graduate of the University of Virginia School of Law. She began her courtroom career as a clerk for a federal judge, the Honorable James M. Burns, in Portland. After clerking, she worked over three years at a well-regarded defense firm where she gained invaluable firsthand knowledge of practices and legal strategies of insurance companies and their defense teams.

A born competitor, Jane attended college on a tennis scholarship. In her first jury trial after becoming a plaintiff's lawyer, she won a verdict over $900,000 on a no-offer personal injury case against a national retailer.

Jane had the honor of serving on the Oregon Trial Lawyers Board 1995-2006, was one of Oregon's two American Trial Lawyer Association Delegates 2000-2004, and was President of OTLA 2004-2005. She is an Associate in the American Board of Trial Advocates and is listed in Best Lawyers in America.

She has also served on the Oregon Law Institute Board and several local and state bar committees including the Oregon State Bar Affirmative Action Committee, the Oregon State Bar Procedure and Practice Committee and the Multnomah Bar Association Judicial Screening Committee. Jane is listed as one of the Best Lawyers in America; an Oregon Super Lawyer, one of Oregon's Top 25 Women Super Lawyers and one of Portland's Best Lawyers in Portland Monthly magazine.

Jane, like all the lawyers in our firm, believes in giving back. She works with and is a Board member of Portland Habitat for Humanity.

attorneys.name: D. Neal Peton Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Keizer, OR
attorneys.bio:
Neal Peton graduated from Willamette University College of Law and was admitted to practice law in 2007. Mr. Peton holds degrees in philosophy and business administration. He is licensed to practice law before the United States Court for the District of Oregon as well as the State Courts of Oregon. Mr. Peton focuses on personal injury and negligence cases. Whether its backpacking, car camping, sea kayaking, snowboarding, or just going for a hike, he enjoys getting out with his family most. When asked what motivates him, Mr. Peton said: “Growing up, I was taught a strong sense of right and wrong, and I think that transferred easily to my legal practice. The tort law is about taking responsibility for mistakes. Insurance companies aren’t always willing to take responsibility for the mistakes of their insureds. My passion is fighting hard to make the responsible party take responsibility for his or her actions. Sometimes insurance companies don’t want to do the right thing. When that happens, I love holding them accountable.”

attorneys.name: John Andrew Pinzelik
attorneys.firm_name: Owens, Sneller, Pinzelik and Wood, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
John Pinzelik was born and raised in West Lafayette, Indiana. After graduating from high school, he moved to California to pursue a career in the music business. John moved to Portland in 1998 and attended law school in the evening while working for various record companies. John joined David W. Owens, P.C. in the spring of 2009 and became a shareholder in the firm in January 2011.

John’s law practice focuses on personal injury and business litigation, wage claims and bankruptcy law. John has helped his clients recover hundreds of thousands of dollars from negligent drivers and property owners. He has prosecuted and defended small businesses in arbitration and state court. John has helped employees recover thousands of dollars in unpaid and penalty wages, and has helped hundreds of clients obtain a financial “fresh start” through the bankruptcy process.

John strives to give every client the attention they deserve and to explain the legal process in way that clients can understand. John believes that it is crucial to understand his client’s needs and to carefully weigh all options before recommending a course of action.

John volunteers with Legal Aid Services of Oregon’s Pro Bono Bankruptcy Clinic and spends his free time biking, running, and playing drums with a local marimba band.

attorneys.name: Jenna Richards
attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense / DUI Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Jenna Richards is a committed criminal defense attorney who focuses on protecting the rights of individuals facing charges at every level of the criminal justice system. Her practice includes representing clients in matters ranging from minor violations and misdemeanors to serious felony and Measure 11 cases. Jenna is known for her thoughtful preparation, clear communication, and strong courtroom advocacy.

Prior to joining Gilroy Napoli Short, Jenna built her defense practice in Washington County, where she handled both court-appointed and privately retained cases. She also played an active role in the county’s Early Case Resolution docket, working to resolve matters efficiently while safeguarding her clients’ long-term interests. With experience appearing in courts throughout Oregon, Jenna brings confidence, professionalism, and adaptability to every case she manages.

Jenna approaches her work with empathy and collaboration, recognizing that each client’s situation is unique. She takes the time to understand her clients’ concerns, explain their options, and develop personalized legal strategies aimed at achieving the most favorable outcomes possible.

She earned her Juris Doctor from Lewis & Clark Law School, graduating in the top 10 percent of her class, and received her Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice, Law & Society from Pacific University, where she graduated summa cum laude. During her academic career, Jenna gained valuable practical experience through internships and volunteer work with the Washington County Juvenile Department, the Metropolitan Public Defender’s Office, and the Oregon Innocence Project.

Outside the office, Jenna enjoys spending time with family and friends, cooking, and exploring nature. Originally from the Bay Area, she also looks forward to visits home and proudly supports her favorite local teams, especially the San Jose Sharks.

attorneys.name: Kathryn S. Root
attorneys.practice_type: Military Divorce Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Kathy is a leading authority on interstate and international custody disputes and provides legal advice and representation in cases involving international family law issues. A powerful litigator and tireless advocate for the interests of families and children, she has a special interest in contested child custody and parenting time disputes. Kathy has substantial experience representing clients in divorce and legal separation cases, including those involving child custody, child and spousal support, and complex property division issues. Kathy has a strong commitment to helping clients through turbulent times by providing reliable legal information and advice focused on each client's needs and desire to find a better future. She has focused her practice on family law for 37 years. A member of the Oregon State Bar Family Law Section, she served for three years on its Executive Committee. She previously served as Chair of the Oregon State Bar's Procedure And Practice Committee and is a former President of the Oregon Academy Of Family Law Practitioners. Kathy is the former Chair of the International Law Committee of the American Bar Association's Family Law Section. Kathy is a past Board member of Oregon Women Lawyers and Oregon Women Lawyers Foundation and is a current member of the Foundation's Advisory Board.

When she's not working, you will often find Kathy on a golf course. She loves the challenge of discovering the nuances of each course she plays.

attorneys.name: David M. Rosen
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bend, OR
attorneys.bio:
David Rosen is the immediate past president of the Oregon State Bar.

He is a founding member and past chair of the Deschutes County Access to Justice Committee and past president of the Oregon Law Foundation and Deschutes County Bar Association. David is honored to have been selected to the oregon super lawyers list for the past several years.

EXPERIENCED CIVIL LITIGATOR AND PERSONAL INJURY ATTORNEY

David began his career in the legal field in 2001, working as an economist for a large, Washington, D.C. firm on the Department of Justice’s RICO case against the Tobacco companies. David would later be hired by that same firm as a summer associate. Upon graduation from law school, he was then hired as an associate assisting in the representation of Fortune 500 companies in the fields of internet service providers, telecommunication companies, and major retailers of household goods.

In 2010 David returned to Central Oregon with his family, where he has exclusively practiced personal injury law since 2011. While many civil attorneys seldom get to court, David has arbitrated and mediated injury and accident cases throughout a good deal of Oregon and tried cases to 12-person juries in Deschutes, Jackson, Josephine, and Klamath counties.

LOCAL LEGAL ADVOCATE

In 2010 David returned to Central Oregon with his family, where he founded High Desert Law and has exclusively practiced personal injury law since 2011. He also offers mediation and arbitration services for personal injury matters that are handled by other attorneys. While many civil attorneys seldom get to court, David has arbitrated and mediated injury and accident cases throughout a good deal of Oregon and tried cases to 12-person juries in Deschutes, Jackson, Josephine, and Klamath counties.

EXPERT LEGAL REPRESENTATION

Leveraging a well-rounded background in law, economics, and damage theories, David combines Big Law training with the heart of a person who has gone through the legal process as a plaintiff. He delivers fierce representation for his clients, drawing from this extensive legal experience to advocate for victims of motor vehicle collisions, bicycle and pedestrian accidents, slip and falls, product liability issues and other negligence. David has successfully negotiated, mediated, settled and arbitrated numerous cases with all the big insurance companies and established a reputation of providing top notch representation in a uniquely compassionate manner.

DAVID'S LEGAL EDUCATION

David attended the University of Maryland School of Law on a full scholarship, where he was mentored by President Jimmy Carter's Attorney General, Benjamin Civiletti. While in law school, David spent a semester working in the United States Senate for Ron Wyden and at the United States Department of Justice, main building. David's undergraduate degree is from the University of Pennsylvania.

attorneys.name: J. William Savage
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lake Oswego, OR
attorneys.bio:
During the last 30 years, J. William (Bill) Savage has represented hundreds of individuals who have suffered serious injuries and trauma from auto accidents, medical negligence, sex abuse and other wrongful acts. Bill has represented people of all ages, from young children to adults, who have been injured or traumatized.

Bill has been successful in recovering millions of dollars in a wide variety of cases. These have included actions against state governments for inadequate supervision of sex offenders, actions against public figures for violence against women, and actions against hospitals and doctors for medical negligence. Bill is an active member in state and national trial lawyer associations.

In 1999, Bill was one of 48 attorneys who were invited to attend Gerry Spence's Trial Lawyers College at the Thunderhead Ranch in Wyoming. The 31-day college brought together some of the best trial lawyers in America, including Morris Dees, Milton Grimes, Paul Luvera and Gerry Spence. The Trial Lawyers College is a personal and professional experience that few trial lawyers have been privileged to attend.

Bill grew up in Seattle, Washington. His father was a tool and die machinist. His mother worked as a secretary at the University of Washington. Bill graduated from the University of Washington in 1973, and he attended law school in Oregon at the Lewis and Clark College, Northwestern School of Law. Bill attained his law degree in 1977.

Bill is admitted to practice in all state and federal courts in Oregon as well as all state courts in the State of Washington, and the US District Court of the Western District of Washington. He is also admitted to practice before the Ninth Circuit, United States Court of Appeals, the Federal Circuit, United States Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court. Bill has been active in local, state and national bar associations. He is listed in Who's Who in American Law and has earned an AV Rating, the top professional rating for both legal skill and integrity, from Martindale-Hubble, the leading lawyer evaluation service in the nation. Bill is a member of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice.

Justice Advocacy Africa, Instructor.

attorneys.name: Karen Schoenfeld
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Hood River, OR
attorneys.bio:
Karen Schoenfeld graduated from St. Johns University School of Law in New York City. After working on Wall Street, she moved to Portland, Oregon to pursue her life’s passions. Since 1992 she has dedicated her professional time to representing the rights of those who are seriously injured in accidents through no fault of their own. She has successfully represented over the years, literally thousands of injury victims from all over the country. While most of her cases were settled with the adverse party’s insurance company, she has also tried many cases over the years to a jury. She strongly believes that part of being a trial lawyer means going to trial when it is necessary to protect the full rights of her clients. She is proud of both her settlements and her large jury verdicts.

Karen also has a side specialty of suing her client’s PIP carriers when they refuse to pay for their medical bills. She gets referrals from doctors and clients because of her aggressive position with regard to insurance companies. When not practicing law, Karen enjoys spending time with her family, painting, reading, cross country skiing, and riding her bicycle in the Columbia River gorge area. She recently organized, along with some friends, a group called the SheBikes dedicated to exploring, on bike, the wonders of the Pacific Northwest.

attorneys.name: Steven M Schoenfeld
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Hood River, OR
attorneys.bio:
Steven Schoenfeld grew up in Queens, NY. He obtained his bachelor’s degree in English Literature from Boston University, graduating in 1986 with honors. He obtained his law degree from St. Johns University in New York City, graduating in 1989. While at St. Johns, he was a regular contributor to the law school newspaper. Also, during law school Mr. Schoenfeld clerked in several local New York law firms, learning the ropes and learning how to litigate cases.

While in law school, Steven met his future wife and law partner to be, Karen, and they moved to Portland, Oregon in 1990. Once in Oregon, Steven began working on personal injury cases and workers' compensation cases for another firm. After approximately one year he set out on his own litigating personal injury and workers' compensation cases.

Since approximately 1990, Mr. Schoenfeld has been specializing in these types of cases. In approximately 1995 his practice became more focused on workers' compensation and employment discrimination cases. At this point, Mr. Schoenfeld has tried well over 1000 workers compensation cases, as he has represented hundreds of clients every year since 1995.

Mr. Schoenfeld is active in the Oregon Bar Association. He is a member of the President's Circle of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association. He is a recently appointed member of the Executive Committee of the Workers' Compensation Section of the Oregon State Bar. He also is a member of the Access to Justice Committee, which advises the State of Oregon and its agencies on providing access to justice to immigrants and minorities.

Mr. Schoenfeld has authored several publications dealing with Oregon workers' compensation laws. He has been a featured speaker at legal seminars for both lawyers and judges dealing with issues relating to workers' compensation.

When not practicing law, Mr. Schoenfeld enjoys playing music with his band of middle aged rock-n-rollers, hiking, cycling, backpacking and skiing steep slopes in Oregon.

attorneys.name: Keith D. Semple
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Eugene, OR
attorneys.bio:
Since 2003, Keith Semple has represented injured workers in Oregon workers’ compensation claims. In that time, he has represented well over a thousand injured workers in every corner of the state, and in all lines of work. Keith pursued a career in law so he could fight for the rights of people who could otherwise be easily outgunned by employers or insurers.

In 2010, Keith added his expertise in workers’ compensation to our team of established attorneys with generations of experience in complex litigation involving catastrophic injury, products liability, and medical negligence. Our combined experience and resources will ensure that every potential claim is considered and every route to recovery is explored.

Keith was raised in rural Illinois. His upbringing in the company of hard working people has given him a sincere and plain spoken approach to helping his clients understand the often complex legal issues involved in their case.

In addition to representing his clients in their individual cases, Keith has become a leading voice at the legislature for the rights of injured workers and reform of the workers’ compensation system. For years, Keith has monitored all the policy developments in the workers’ compensation arena, and has helped harness and coordinate the efforts of those who support injured workers. For this work, Keith was honored with the 2020 Doug Swanson Outstanding Workers’ Compensation Attorney Award by the prior recipients of that award. Keith’s engagement on these issues helps him stay abreast of any changes or developments in the law, sometimes even before they take effect.

In his spare time, Keith enjoys spending time outside with his family taking hikes, teaching his kids to ride bikes and working on his yard and garden. In the winter, Keith enjoys skiing, and hopes to get his kids on the slopes someday. Keith is also a novice photographer, and took the firm pictures featured on the website.

attorneys.name: Alexis Shimada
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Salem, OR
attorneys.bio:
Alexis received her undergraduate degree in Sociology and Anthropology from University of Redlands in 2014. Alexis graduated from Willamette University College of Law in 2017.

During law school, she externed at the Marion County Circuit Court for a summer and clerked at a local Salem firm for two and half years focusing on post-conviction relief. She was a legal intern for the Child and Family Advocacy Clinic at Willamette, which allowed her to work with low-income individuals providing pro bono services for dissolutions and adoptions. She gained valuable experience in drafting pleadings and motions and in client communication. Alexis was also actively involved in organizations involving minorities, and is the former President of the National Asian Pacific American Law Students Association.

Alexis served as a Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) for Marion County, from 2018-2023. Alexis’ motivation to become a CASA stems from her belief that no one should have to endure physical or emotional abuse. She believes that all members of a family should live in a loving and stable environment. These beliefs transfer to her passion to ensure that everyone has access to the legal system to make sure they are safe and their children are safe. She strongly believes that everyone deserves to have a voice and is committed to making that happen.

When she is not working, she enjoys Crossfit and teaching Crossfit classes, and spending time with her dogs, Java and Diego.

attorneys.name: Jason Short
attorneys.firm_name: Gilroy Napoli Short Law Group LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense/ DUI Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Jason Short is a seasoned Oregon trial attorney who represents clients in criminal defense and complex legal matters statewide. Before founding Short Law Group, P.C., he served nearly eight years as a Deputy District Attorney, where he tried more than 160 cases before juries and judges and handled over 6,000 matters ranging from DUII and misdemeanor charges to serious felony and Measure 11 prosecutions. He also interned with the United States Attorney’s Office, gaining federal courtroom experience. His background as a former prosecutor—and his work training law enforcement on search and seizure law—gives him strategic insight into how cases are investigated, charged, and tried.

Drawing on that extensive courtroom experience, Jason provides aggressive, results-driven criminal defense representation, including DUI defense, felony defense, and gun rights restoration. He has even represented fellow attorneys facing criminal charges, reflecting the trust placed in his advocacy skills. Recognized for his trial ability and professional reputation, Jason was selected in 2014, 2015, and 2016 to The National Trial Lawyers: Top 100 Criminal Defense Trial Lawyers, an invitation-only distinction honoring leading trial attorneys nationwide. As a certified pistol instructor and member of the National Rifle Association, he is particularly knowledgeable in firearm law and gun rights restoration cases.

Born in Washington and raised in Salem, Jason returned to Oregon after college to earn his law degree from Willamette University College of Law. He is married with four children and is active in his community. Outside the courtroom, he enjoys golf, fishing, racquetball, hiking, camping, and is proud to be an Eagle Scout—values that reflect the discipline, integrity, and dedication he brings to every client’s case.

attorneys.name: Dave Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Banking & Finance Law Lawyers in West Linn, OR
attorneys.bio:
Dave Smith exemplifies the intent of this firm, to care for businesses as people. His experience in advising businesses, contractors, and property owners on transactional matters, as well as handling a wide array of litigation cases, serves as a foundation for what this firm means to its clients and to its community.

Dave focuses his practice on resolving business and construction disputes. David also advises businesses, contractors, and property owners on transactional matters involving corporate formation and governance, real estate, contract negotiation, and employment matters.

Dave has successfully resolved product liability cases, construction litigation, UCC debtor/creditor disputes, employment issues, lien and bond claims, and intellectual property matters. Dave also has extensive experience representing insurance companies and property owners in the recovery of losses due to property damage. Dave's experience in trial, arbitration, mediation, and settlement negotiations enables him to advise businesses on the many issues that arise under federal and state statutes, or under contract, both to avoid litigation and to ensure a strong defense in the event of a lawsuit.

Dave has gained his experience in solving complex commercial disputes while representing a wide range of clients, including financial institutions, contractors, developers, property owners, securities brokers, product manufacturers, insurance companies, and business professionals. Combined with his diverse litigation background, Dave's in-depth knowledge of the legal process enables him to assist his clients in solving disputes that otherwise get in the way of what they know best -- business.

Knowing that the best results depend on the expectations of the client and that each matter may have a different goal, he ensures that each client is provided the level of service required. David has:

Successfully represented through trial a general contractor in a Federal Court Miller Act lawsuit.

Represented a consulting firm in a $100 million complex professional malpractice lawsuit that was ultimately mediated with a favorable result for the client.

Co-arbitrated a National Association of Securities Dealers securities arbitration that resulted in a dismissal of all claims against the client.

Represented a variety of manufacturers and high-tech companies in intellectual property disputes over trademarks, trade dress, and copyrights.

Represented owners, contractors, developers, engineers, and design professionals in all facets of construction-related litigation, including trial, arbitration, and mediation.

Prosecuted ten jury trials as an acting assistant district attorney.

Successfully represented insurance companies and their insureds in all facets of disputes, including liability, coverage, subrogation, and inter-company claims.

Successfully arbitrated numerous subrogation claims on behalf of insurance companies.

attorneys.practice_type: Probate Lawyers in Tualatin, OR
attorneys.bio:
Susan Snell was born and raised in Oregon. She earned her Bachelor of Science Degree from Portland State University in 1982, and earned her Doctorate of Jurisprudence from Lewis and Clark Law School in Portland, Oregon in 1985. She was admitted to the Oregon State Bar and United States District Court for the District of Oregon in 1985 and to the Washington State Bar in 2021. Susan has practiced law in Tualatin, Oregon since 1988.

Susan is primarily a transactional attorney. For 40 years, she values helping people in challenging times, whether it is guiding families and loved ones through the probate system or minimizing anxiety by simply answering questions. She prides herself on being approachable, reliable and down to earth. She also strives to provide a helping hand whom her clients can turn to for guidance and support by taking the mystery out of the legal process. Susan’s practice emphasizes legal issues unique to the elderly and their families, including guardianship and conservatorship proceedings, probate estates, trust administration, and estate planning.

attorneys.name: Judy Danelle Snyder
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Judy Snyder
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Lake Oswego, OR
attorneys.bio:
Judy Snyder has been a trial attorney for more than 40 years. Because of the significant number of cases she has litigated, her firm routinely represents clients in a wide variety of areas of civil litigation - personal injury, medical negligence, legal negligence, wrongful death, employment and civil rights. Although most of Judy’s skills are devoted to representing individuals who are pursuing claims for damages, it is common for her to represent individuals and small businesses who have been sued - successfully defending and aggressively pursuing claims against the parties who filed the litigation. Her cases are filed in the state and federal courts throughout the state of Oregon. As a result of her experience, Judy regularly represents licensed professionals - doctors, psychologists, nurses - before their licensing boards.

After Judy graduated from the University of Notre Dame School of Law, she moved to Oregon to clerk for U.S. District Court Judge Otto R. Skopil. Judy then became an aggressive and effective prosecuting attorney in the Multnomah County District Attorney’s Office. In 1978, Judy opened her law firm which focuses on civil litigation in the federal and state courts throughout the state of Oregon.

In 2001, the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association honored Judy with its Distinguished Trial Lawyer Award. Earlier in 2001, the Oregon State Bar Litigation Section awarded her the Owen M. Panner Professionalism Award. In 2009, Judy was awarded the Multnomah Bar Professionalism Award. Most recently, she received the 2025 Burns Federal Civil Practice Award from the Oregon Chapter of the Federal Bar Association.

In 2008, Judy became a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA). ABOTA is an invitation-only organization for civil trial attorneys who have significant trial experience and who demonstrate civility, integrity and professionalism in their practice. And, in 2016, she became a member of the American College of Trial Attorneys, which is an invitation-only organization limited to no more than 1% of the attorneys in any State.

Judy has also been recognized by the legal publications Super Lawyers and Best Lawyers. She has a Martindale-Hubble AV Preeminent rating from her peers. Judy also has served as a leader in numerous professional associations and volunteer boards and agencies. From 1989 to 1990, she served as president of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association. From 1999 to 2000, she served as president of the Multnomah County Bar Association. She has also been a long-time member of the American Association for Justice, the National Employment Lawyers Association, the Federal Bar Association, and has been active with committees and in various positions with the Oregon State Bar Association.

Judy frequently serves as a presenter at Continuing Education programs for attorneys throughout the state. She lectures several times a year on various aspects of trial practice, evidence, trial techniques, and substantive law issues.

Judy’s community activities have included a four-year term on the State of Oregon’s Psychiatric Security Review Board where she was the Chair from 1983 to 1984. She then served on the State of Oregon's Board of Psychologist Examiners from 1986 to 1988. She previously served on the Board of Trustees of Jesuit High School. Judy presently serves on the Commission for Judicial Fitness and Disability.

attorneys.name: Brian Stimson
attorneys.firm_name: DuBois Law Group - PDX Injury Law
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
From the beginning of his legal career, Brian has specialized in personal injury and Portland wrongful death litigation. Brian is a skilled advocate inside and outside the courtroom, and truly enjoys helping people through the most difficult parts of their lives. He knows firsthand the fear, pain, and uncertainty that people go through after an injury. Understanding that experience is key to building valuable personal injury cases.

Brian is active in the legal community, and is an elected, voting member of the Oregon State Bar House of Delegates, Region 5. He also belongs to the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association, Washington State Association for Justice, and American Association for Justice. He is licensed in Oregon state and federal courts, Washington state courts, and admitted in Minnesota.

He graduated from the Mitchell Hamline School of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota before returning to his home in Oregon to practice with DuBois Law Group - PDX Injury Law. During law school, he was a Bakken Fellow, Honor Roll recipient, and frequent mock trial/moot court competitor. He clerked for two years as a student attorney for the Hennepin County District Attorney’s office where he gained experience in the courtroom, working on civil and criminal cases. He also clerked and worked closely with Senior Ramsey County Judge Judith Tilsen.

Before he became a Portland injury attorney, Brian was an award-winning newspaper journalist for several Portland-area papers. He attended the Mayborn School of Journalism at the University of North Texas, where he served as the editor-in-chief of the North Texas Daily newspaper.

Outside the office, Brian spends much of his time with his wife and young son. He enjoys building Legos and taking his son to the park. He is also an avid outdoorsman and has reached the summit of both Mt. Hood and Mt. Adams.

attorneys.name: Kevin D. Swartz
attorneys.firm_name: Kevin D Swartz Attorney at Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Lawyers in Salem, OR
attorneys.bio: I am grateful for my career. I have been practicing for close to 20 years helping clients with complex cases to those that are simple and straight-forward. I am grateful for the level of trust my clients place in me and do not take it lightly. My favorite moments are when I get to see the look of relief in my clients eyes knowing that the financial issues they have been struggling with (many for years and years) are behind them. I am also grateful for the ability to turn someone's life around in as little as 90 days. I am a planner. I ask my client's "Where do you want to be in 3 years?" Sometimes my representation only takes 90-days but we go beyond cleaning up the mess to planning for the future. That can include credit repair/rebuilding all the way to discussing how to build an emergency fund or qualify to buy a house. I view what I call the "planning phase" as the fun part clients and I get to do when their case is over. I love numbers. This goes hand-in-hand with the planner in me. I like to detail out client's budgets and then talk to them about their future. Most clients are trying to get in a financial position where they can qualify to buy a house. I am amazed how many create their own mental blocks and think they will never qualify. I love being able to run the numbers and go over the steps so they have a plan of action to start on that very day.

attorneys.name: Chloe Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Bend, OR
attorneys.bio:
Chloe is a second-generation personal injury lawyer and a committed advocate for Central Oregonians who are harmed as a result of negligent defendants. She provides aggressive legal representation and works diligently to achieve the best possible results for her clients. She is honored to have been selected to the Superlawyers Rising Stars list for 2024.

OREGON INJURY ATTORNEY

Chloe grew up on a cattle ranch in Crook County and attended the University of Oregon where she graduated with a Bachelor of Arts. After college Chloe was employed at two civil litigation firms in California before moving to Portland where she worked at a personal injury firm leading up to and during law school. There she had the opportunity to assist on a wrongful death lawsuit in Eastern Oregon which resulted in a $26.5 million jury verdict. Chloe has gained valuable experience working on a variety of cases including those involving dog bites, sexual assault, medical malpractice, products liability, and premises liability as well as collisions involving pedestrians, bicyclists, motor vehicles, commercial trucks, trains, airplanes, helicopters, and boats. Chloe is a graduate of Willamette University College of Law.

Outside of work, Chloe loves spending time with her friends and family. She also enjoys world travel (she has been to 32 countries), hiking, riding horses, drinking craft beer, and going to concerts.

attorneys.name: Jana Triska
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Jana’s client-centered practice focuses on estate planning, estate and trust administration, probate, and transactional business law.

Prior to Chenoweth Law Group LLC, Jana worked as general counsel in start-up business and in her own firm specializing in transactional entertainment, business law, and intellectual property law in Los Angeles. After moving to Portland, Jana worked in an estate planning firm and found her passion for counseling clients regarding estate planning and administration.

Jana enjoys working with individuals and families to craft solid estate plans to ensure their loved ones receive their intended gifts upon passing while avoiding family disputes over distributions. Jana counsels clients on strategies to minimize taxes and protect and conserve assets. Jana takes great care to clearly communicate her advice to clients, while firmly believing it's just as important to listen to clients as it is to advise them. She has a passion for clarity and plain-language agreements to ensure her clients understand any proposed plan or action.

Estate planning is a sensitive area of law and Jana’s compassionate yet direct approach helps put people at ease when discussing money and delicate family matters.

attorneys.name: Scarlett A. Van Syoc
attorneys.practice_type: High Asset Divorce Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Scarlett is a compassionate and dedicated family law attorney with a profound understanding of the emotional turmoil that clients experience during family law litigation. With Scarlett's empathetic approach, clients can find solace in knowing that their every concern will be acknowledged and addressed throughout the legal process. With well over a decade of family law experience, much of it spent in the courtrooms of New York City, Scarlett has honed the skill of identifying whether a case will be best served by a gentle approach or an aggressive one.

Known for her ability to navigate the complex intersection of law and emotions, Scarlett helps clients make clear and informed decisions for their future. By providing guidance and support, Scarlett ensures that clients have a solid foundation to build a brighter future upon.

In addition to her expertise in family law, Scarlett brings a unique perspective to each case. She describes herself as having the remarkable ability to find humor in any situation, which can help alleviate tension and foster positive communication. This, combined with her tenacity and extroverted nature, allows Scarlett to connect with clients on a personal level and build strong relationships based on trust and understanding.

One of the most important lessons Scarlett has learned throughout her career is that being the loudest voice in the room doesn't necessarily equate to being the voice heard. Scarlett firmly believes in the power of thoughtful communication and emphasizes the impact of words before they are spoken. This wisdom guides her interactions with clients, opposing counsel, and the court, ensuring that every word spoken is purposeful and productive.

Beyond the courtroom, Scarlett enjoys various hobbies that enrich her life and bring balance to their profession. She is an avid cook, constantly exploring new and interesting cuisines. Scarlett also devotes her time to animal rescue and volunteering. She finds joy in swimming, hiking, indulging in reality shows on Bravo (a guilty pleasure), and cherishing moments spent with her own rescue pitbull, Quinn.

With Scarlett's combination of empathy, legal expertise, and a genuine passion for helping clients, she is well-equipped to guide individuals through the challenges of family law and create a positive path forward for their clients' lives.

attorneys.bio:
For Charles, being a great family law attorney is about empowering people to find strength during life’s most adverse moments. He views his role as an advocate, helping each client with their unique situation. He believes there is no form fitting or cookie cutter resolution that is going to work for each client. His loyal, well-grounded nature has taught him there is no replacement for attention to detail and careful preparation, and that success is always a byproduct of great collaborative effort. Charles is the ultimate team player helping clients navigate the legal system while helping them become stronger, happier individuals.

For fun, Charles enjoys reading science fiction/fiction, biking, and photography. If he could live anywhere in the world he would choose Costa Rica or Hawaii as both locations embody the idea that the path is as important as the result. When it comes to personal and professional growth, Charles believes the path towards obtaining a goal is often as important as obtaining the goal itself.

Charles is the ultimate team player helping clients navigate the legal system while helping them become stronger, happier individuals.

For fun, Charles enjoys reading science fiction/fiction, biking, and photography. If he could live anywhere in the world he would choose Costa Rica or Hawaii as both locations embody the idea that the path is as important as the result. When it comes to personal and professional growth, Charles believes the path towards obtaining a goal is often as important as obtaining the goal itself.

I am dedicated to you, the client. At all stages of the legal process I will honor your legal, personal, economic needs . At all stages I will collaborate with you so that your needs are met and your experience with the legal system is an empowering one.

I was born and raised in Central and Eastern Oregon. This part of the country will always be my first home. I feel lucky to have a great family and consider my husband, my parents, my two brothers and my sister amongst my best friends.

As a criminal defense attorney I get to do the things which matter most to me: help people in meaningful and tangible ways and rise to varied and interesting challenges.

When I am not working I love to play in the out of doors! I spend my free time climbing, rafting, trail running, reading or gardening with my husband Kevin.

attorneys.name: Linda Weimar
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury and Property Damage Lawyers in Beaverton, OR
attorneys.bio:
Over the past several years, Linda Weimar has been and continues to be committed to providing successful and compassionate representation to her clients. When individuals have suffered injury due to the wrongful acts of another, are going through a divorce, or are facing other legal issues, it is important to hire a lawyer who they feel comfortable with and who has the experience and aggressiveness to advocate for their rights both in the courtroom and outside the courtroom.

Linda was born in Oregon and she and her husband and daughter have lived in the Portland / Beaverton area for the past 25 years. She has close ties with and a love of the Bend area, where her parents and a sister have lived for more than 20 years. The Weimar clan has resided in the Oregon and Idaho area for generations.

Linda graduated from Northwestern School of Law, Lewis & Clark College in 1997 in the top third of her class while attending law school at night, working nearly full-time during the day, and raising a toddler.

Over the years since law school, Linda has represented hundreds of individuals who have suffered injuries and trauma from auto accidents, animal attacks, unsafe premises, medical negligence and other wrongful acts.

Linda is licensed to practice law in both Oregon and Washington. She is a member of several local, state and national bar associations, including a President's Circle member of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Natalie M. Wetenhall
attorneys.practice_type: Wills and Estates Lawyers in Ashland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Natalie offers an extensive range of tailored estate planning packages at competitive prices. Her estate planning practice ranges from the preparation of simple last will and testaments, to the creation of complex revocable and irrevocable trusts, as well as business succession planning, durable financial power of attorneys, advance medical directives, and a variety of other helpful estate planning tools.

In her business practice, Natalie provides legal services for entrepreneurs, investors and companies of all sizes throughout the states of California, Oregon and Washington. She focuses her practice on establishing and maintaining corporations, LLCs and other business entities, regulatory compliance, day-to-day operations as they relate to business, as well as more complex business transactions, including membership and shareholder buy-outs, purchase and sale of a business, mergers and acquisitions, restructuring, intellectual property protection, and counseling and representing clients in general contract negotiations, dispute resolution and a variety of business transactional matters.

Prior to co-forming Evergreen Law Group, LLC, Natalie practiced for several years as a corporate business transactional attorney in New York City. She worked at the worldwide headquarters of JPMorgan Chase Bank, in the legal department of its Investment Banking Division, where she drafted and negotiated institutional-level commercial loan agreements, as well as a wide range of derivative trading agreements for prime brokerage and other corporate clients. Natalie also practiced in the Capital Markets group of 'Biglaw' firm Davis Polk and Wardwell LLP, where she led a team of associates on a major restructuring project for a prestigious hedge fund client, in addition to drafting and negotiating the full suite of prime brokerage client contracts and business transactional agreements for hedge fund and investment bank clients.

Natalie received her law degrees in both Civil and Common Law (J.D.) from McGill University in 2001. Before commencing law school, she received her B.A. in Honors English, graduating Magna cum laude, from McGill University. Natalie is an active Member of the Ashland Rotary, the acting Vice President of the Jackson County Bar Association, and is a continued Benefactor of the Schneider Museum of Art in Ashland. When she is not working, Natalie loves to hike, ski, play the piano with her son, enjoy the local wineries, and attend Oregon Shakespeare Festival performances.

attorneys.name: Robert W. Wilkinson
attorneys.practice_type: Community Associations Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Rob Wilkinson is a construction attorney with almost 25 years of experience handling construction defect and property damage claims. He has successfully prosecuted construction defect claims for the owners of single-family homes, apartments, condominiums, hotels, retirement centers, municipal and school district properties, and commercial buildings.\

In addition to construction defect claims, Rob drafts and negotiates construction and design contracts, and handles disputes that may arise during the course of construction.

Rob has written articles on construction law and is a frequent speaker on construction topics. He serves as an arbitrator with the Arbitration Service of Portland. He is a member of the Construction Sections of the Oregon State Bar and the American Bar Association, the Inns of Court, and the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association, where he serves on the Publication Committee. He is also a member of Community Association Institute’s Education Committee and the Multnomah Bar Association’s Solo and Small Firm Committee. Rob devotes volunteer time to Legal Aid Services of Oregon, representing victims of domestic violence in contested restraining order hearings. Rob has been on the Oregon Super Lawyers list annually going back to 2015, and has been listed in Best Lawyers in America every year since 2018.

Rob got his start in construction during college, working for a small general contractor. After college, Rob was in the U.S. Peace Corps in the Islamic Republic of Mauritania, and then worked in New Mexico with at-risk youth. Rob graduated from the University of Oregon Law School and followed that with a clerkship for a federal judge in Portland. Rob then worked for almost 22 years in construction law at the Ball Janik law firm. In January 2023, Rob and Nels Vulin established Vulin Wilkinson LLC, focusing on construction and construction defect matters. Rob lives with his family in Portland.

attorneys.name: Tim Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Bend, OR
attorneys.bio:
Tim Williams is our lead litigation attorney. Tim is particularly skilled at jury trials, and has tried a number of cases to verdict. In fact, Tim has taken more cases to trial than most of his peers. He has a reputation for his tenacity, competence, and professionalism among the legal community.

Tim handles all types of personal injury cases, including car accidents, semi-truck accidents, ATV and motorcycle accidents, airline injuries, slip and falls, work accidents, animal attacks, neck and back injuries / whiplash / herniated disks, brain injuries, nerve injuries, bone and joint injuries, neck and back surgeries, wrongful death, and much more. Given his litigation experience, Tim is able to settle most of his cases without the need for trial. However, Tim never assumes a case will settle out of court, loves trial work, and prepares each case accordingly.

Tim Williams was born and raised in Grants Pass, Oregon. He attended Grants Pass High School from 1991-1995, where he was a standout athlete in football, basketball, and track. He graduated with Honors in 1995.

Tim attended Linfield College in McMinnville, Oregon in 1995-1996. While at Linfield, he played basketball for the college and focused his studies on Chemistry. He then attended Southern Oregon University in Ashland, Oregon from 1996-1999, where he played college football and basketball. His 1998-1999 college basketball team ranked second in the nation during the season, won the Conference Championship, and played in the National Tournament. While attending SOU, Tim worked weekends and summers at a plywood mill in Grants Pass (Stone Forest, later U.S. Forest Products). He graduated with Honors, Summa Cum Laude, from SOU with a Bachelor of Science degree in Criminology in 1999.

Tim began working at Roy Dwyer's personal injury firm as a law clerk in the fall of 1999, where he continued working throughout law school. He attended the University of Oregon School of Law from 2000-2003. While there, he was active in his role as student liaison for the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association, and worked for Lane County Legal Aid representing low-income clients in civil disputes. He graduated from the University of Oregon School of Law in 2003, and was admitted to the Oregon State Bar the same year. He now focuses his statewide law practice on personal injury litigation, and is the primary litigation attorney for the firm.

Tim lives in Bend, Oregon with his wife and daughter. Aside from spending time with his family, Tim enjoys hiking, mountain biking, golfing, fishing, hunting, wakeboarding, and playing basketball. He particularly enjoys snowboarding on Mt. Bachelor. Tim also volunteers to help the less fortunate in the community, including several Rotary projects, and also serving on the board of the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Central Oregon.

attorneys.bio:
Kristin believes that family is the most important aspect of our lives—and when change happens it is hard to see beyond the immediate conflict. Her primary goal is to help clients navigate difficult times and find the right solution so they can move forward. Those who have worked with Kristin can attest to her practical problem solving skills, efficient work ethic, and ability to find common ground with people of all walks of life. Her well-grounded and optimistic nature have taught her there is no replacement for careful preparation, and that success is usually a bi-product of great collaborative effort. Kristin is dedicated to helping her clients understand the complex family legal process and ultimately bringing peace of mind to each person, and family, she represents.

When not in the office, I’ll likely find Kristin adventuring throughout the pacific northwest; hiking in the mountains or somewhere near the water, playing board games with friends or enjoying a great glass of Oregon pinot noir.

attorneys.bio:
Joseph M. Winsby ("Joe") is an AV Preeminent rated trial attorney. Joe has extensive experience successfully representing clients in high-stakes and complex matters from the pre-suit investigation phase through jury trial and arbitration in diverse areas of the law that range from insurance coverage, commercial litigation, construction defect, and premises liability. Joe pays meticulous attention to detail without sacrificing the importance of being a common sense and big-picture lawyer. He is licensed in Oregon, Washington, and Florida.

Joe is a Trial College Fellow of the American Board of Trial Advocates’ National Trial College at Harvard Law School. He graduated from the University of Miami School of Law, ranking cum laude among his classmates and receiving an honors distinction from the nationally acclaimed Litigation Skills program.

In 2021, Joe and his wife and two young daughters made the decision to move to the Pacific Northwest to be closer to their extended family and explore the outdoors. Before joining CLG, Joe was the managing partner of the Oregon and Washington offices of a mid-sized insurance defense firm, and a partner in a boutique litigation firm in Coral Gables, Florida.

attorneys.name: Sara A. Winter
attorneys.practice_type: Asset Protection Planning Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Sara has a natural talent of instantly connecting with people. Both personally and professionally, building great relationships has always been the cornerstone of her success. Whether she is helping clients plan for their future or guiding them through the loss of a loved one, her goal is to give clients comfort that their loved ones are taken care of, preserve their legacy, and achieve their goals. Knowing each client has different needs, and complexity of estate planning work, she strives to ensure each client understands the work being done—and more importantly, the mission behind it—in a practical and sensitive manner. With an LL.M. in Taxation, Sara uses her expertise to place a special focus on tax planning for all of her clients, whether it is income, gift, or estate related.

Sara relocated to Portland after a decade of building a successful estate planning practice in Houston, Texas. When she’s not helping clients plan for their future, you’ll likely find Sara running, baking, or spending time with her husband, their son, and their French Bulldog, Butters.

Her professional motto is "Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much." –Helen Keller

attorneys.name: Brook D. Wood
attorneys.firm_name: Owens, Sneller, Pinzelik and Wood, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning & Probate Lawyers in Portland, OR
attorneys.bio:
Brook D. Wood is licensed to practice law in Oregon. Already a law clerk with David W. Owens, P.C. & Associates while in law school, Brook joined the ranks of the firm’s attorneys after being admitted to the bar in October of 2009, and became a shareholder in January of 2011.

Brook graduated from the University of Arizona in Tucson, Arizona, in 2002 with a Bachelor’s of Science in Ecology & Evolutionary Biology. He received his Juris Doctor from the Lewis and Clark Law School here in Portland, having never visited the state of Oregon before deciding to attend there.

Brook’s practice focuses on civil litigation and motions practice, contract drafting, review, and enforcement, and estate planning, probate, and administration. His practice has primarily been in the State Circuit Courts for the counties of Clackamas and Multnomah, and he is admitted to practice in the Federal District Court for the District of Oregon. Whatever the issue, Brook is committed to providing his clients with the knowledge, skill, and communication necessary to bring satisfactory resolution to their complex and trying problems.

Brook brings a broad perspective to the practice of law, having come to the law as a second career. Prior to enrolling in law school, Brook worked in an entomology laboratory at the University of Arizona, collecting data on hereditary resistance development in pests of transgenic cotton and co-authoring several publications on the subject. His background in the sciences has helped him develop the analytical skills necessary to evaluate fact patterns and wade through complex statutory language. Brook’s wide interests have also influenced his development as an attorney and as a person. He has served on the boards of directors of charity organizations supporting the arts and the environment and has been involved with groups like the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, the United Way, and Habitat for Humanity.

Away from the law, Brook enjoys sports and exploring all that Oregon and the Pacific Northwest has to offer with his wife and their dogs.
